items.model: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 25829ST.OO.0944ST.01 Stainless Steel Openworked Dial (1994)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Few watches conceal such mechanical sophistication behind an unassuming façade as the steel  Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar. Skeletonizing a perpetual calendar ranks among the painstaking feats in watchmaking, demanding that each component be hand-pierced and bevelled without compromising the mechanism’s integrity. Audemars Piguet achieves that in this openworked Royal Oak, transforming its complication into a transparent window onto horological artistry. The result is remarkable for appearing in stainless steel rather than precious metal, an unexpected pairing that heightens its appeal. Rare and dazzling, this reference stands as a connoisseur’s trophy within the Royal Oak lineage.

 The 39mm stainless steel case frames an openworked dial that lays the perpetual calendar’s mechanism bare, exposing the bridges, wheels, and gears. Blued hands and subdials trace the calendar across the transparency: weekday at nine, date at three, month and leap-year above, and a moon phase at six. A week scale encircles the display. The octagonal bezel and steel bracelet anchor this spectacle in the Royal Oak idiom, balancing theatre with wearability.

 *This timepiece comes with AP Digital Archive Papers.

Audemars Piguet's Cobra belongs to a golden age of 1970s dress watchmaking, when the great houses wrapped slim movements in flowing precious-metal bracelets. Named for the flexible, snake-like mesh that hugs the wrist, it channels an era of effortless, sun-kissed glamour. This all-yellow-gold example is a study in warm monochrome, its champagne dial melting into the woven gold bracelet for a seamless, jewelry-first effect. Collectors prize the Cobra as elegant, understated luxury that rewards true discernment.

 Measuring a refined 27 millimeters, the cushion-shaped yellow gold case sits flush within its integrated woven mesh bracelet, the two flowing together as one continuous sculpture. The RM 35-03 ' Rafael Nadal ' is the latest chapter, introducing a variable-geometry butterfly rotor that lets its owner fine-tune the automatic winding with a simple switch. Dressed in cheerful pastel blue with a rainbow of coloured accents, it channels the champion's exuberance into a wearable feat of engineering.

 The tonneau case is formed from Quartz TPT, a feather-light composite prized for resisting shock, here in a soft sky-blue finish trimmed with a pink ring and deep blue crown. Its skeletonised movement fills the dial, gears and bridges suspended in open space for the eye to explore. A selector at three switches between winding, neutral, and hand-setting, an ON/OFF indicator sits above six, and a navy rubber strap anchors it.

A small round case anchors one end, its bezel engraved with the double "BVLGARI BVLGARI" logo that became a brand hallmark. items.sourceDescription:
The  RM 030 embodies Richard Mille's obsession with mechanical problem-solving, built around one of the brand's cleverest innovations: a declutchable rotor that can be disengaged at will, halting automatic winding so the wearer can prevent the mainspring from over-tensioning. This "Black Out" version, produced exclusively for the Americas in a run of just thirty pieces, cloaks that technical brilliance in a wholly blacked-out aesthetic, making it one of the rarest and most coveted regional editions Richard Mille has created.

 The tonneau-shaped case is machined from grade-5 titanium and finished in matte black DLC, its bezel secured by Richard Mille's signature spline screws. The skeletonized movement is laid bare, its bridges and gears blacked out to match, with white-tipped hands and applied numerals cutting through the darkness. An oversized date sits at six o'clock and a function indicator reveals the rotor's status, while a black rubber strap completes this purpose-built machine.

 *This is a limited edition of 30 pieces.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Among connoisseurs, F.P.Journe occupies a singular place, and the Chronomètre à Résonance is arguably his most celebrated creation. It harnesses a rare physical phenomenon: two independent movements, beating side by side, that naturally synchronize through acoustic resonance to improve stability and precision. Few watchmakers in history have tamed this principle for the wrist, and Journe's mastery of it has made the Résonance a grail among serious collectors, an intellectual object as much as a beautiful one.

 Cased in platinum with a matching bracelet, the current Calibre 1520 measures in a 40mm case and glows with a solid gold dial in warm salmon. Two subdials display the time twice, twelve-hour right and twenty-four-hour left, flanking the twin resonating balances at the center. A power reserve arcs across the top, small seconds sit below, and a pair of remontoirs d'égalité feed constant force to each gear train, rendered in Journe's inimitable hand.

items.sourceDescription:
The 5726A-001 expanded the  Nautilus into more complicated territory when it debuted in 2010, marrying Gérald Genta's iconic 1976 sports design with Patek Philippe's patented annual calendar. The annual calendar itself — a Patek invention of 1996 — represents one of the maison's signature contributions to modern watchmaking, automatically accounting for months of thirty and thirty-one days while requiring correction only once a year. For collectors, the reference offers a compelling balance: the everyday wearability and unmistakable identity of the Nautilus combined with a genuinely useful complication, executed in steel and offered on a leather strap rather than the familiar integrated bracelet.

 The 40.5mm case in stainless steel measures 11.3mm thick, retaining the signature rounded octagonal bezel with alternating satin and polished finishes. The sunburst charcoal grey dial with black-gradient rim carries horizontal embossing, white gold applied baton markers, and luminescent hands, with day, date, and month apertures beneath twelve and a combined moon phase and 24-hour subdial at six. The Grand Complications 5270G-018 occupies landmark status in modern Patek Philippe history as the maison's very first in-house perpetual calendar chronograph — introduced in 2011 as the culmination of decades of movement development that finally freed Patek from its reliance on modified Lémania ébauches for its most prestigious chronograph complications. Perpetual calendar chronographs have long ranked among the most coveted and collectible wristwatches in the entire market — appearing on more auction catalogue covers than any other watch type — making the 5270G-018 an instant landmark upon its release. Produced only from 2011 through late 2013 before being superseded by the -013 variant with a redesigned dial, this first-series reference has since attained particular collector distinction, identified through its distinctive black gold indexes.

 The 41mm case in 18-karat white gold measures 12.4mm thick, featuring a concave bezel, two-tier lugs, and sapphire display caseback revealing the movement. The silvery opaline dial displays black gold indexes, day and month double apertures at twelve, moon phase and date-by-hand at six, thirty-minute chronograph counter at three, small seconds at nine, and day/night and leap year indicators. The hand-wound Caliber CH 29-535 PS Q — a 456-part column-wheel chronograph with silent operation and six patented innovations — delivers a 65-hour power reserve, completed by a black hand-stitched alligator strap with 18-karat white gold fold-over clasp.

Arnold Schwarzenegger became the line's most famous champion, and this rose gold chronograph edition celebrates that bond, created to support his After-School All-Stars charity for at-risk youth. Limited to just 350 pieces, it fuses genuine philanthropy with serious collector cachet. Enthusiasts treasure it as a rare, storied, purpose-driven Offshore. 

 Rende red in 18-karat rose gold, the 48mm case carries the Offshore's octagonal bezel with eight exposed screws, paired with an inner tachymeter scale. The brown Méga Tapisserie dial layers three chronograph counters and a date at three over its checkerboard texture, lit by applied rose gold Arabic numerals and matching hands. Twin rectangular pushers flank the crown. Driven by an automatic chronograph movement, it rides on a black rubber strap, muscular and unmistakably Offshore. 

 *This is a limited edition of 350 pieces.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Greubel Forsey occupies a singular place in contemporary haute horlogerie as one of the most uncompromising independents — founded by Robert Greubel and Stephen Forsey in 2004 and renowned for inventions like the Quadruple Tourbillon, the Double Tourbillon 30°, and a standard of 100% hand-finishing rarely matched at any price. The Balancier 3, introduced in late 2023 and produced from 2024 through 2028, represents the atelier's most accessible entry into its world — limited to just 88 pieces per colorway, the result of nearly twenty years of consideration. It distills the brand's full technical and finishing language into a more direct, sports-oriented expression, characterized by three architecturally suspended bridges and a 12.6mm variable-inertia balance wheel — among the largest in contemporary watchmaking.

 The 41.5mm Convexe case in titanium measures 13.35mm thick, the lugs unscrewed for the first time in Greubel Forsey's history and profiled to follow the wrist's natural curvature. The openworked black dial displays the balance wheel at five, fast-rotating barrels at one and ten, small seconds at eight beneath a fixed red triangle, and an arch bridge carrying the hour and minute hands. The hand-wound in-house caliber comprises 282 parts and 43 jewels seated in olived gold chatons, delivering a 72-hour chronometric reserve via twin coupled barrels, completed by a rubber strap with titanium folding clasp.

 *This is a limited edition of 88 pieces.

 *The retail price of this watch is $228,000.

 *This timepiece is complete, and comes with a loop.

items.model: Rolex Deepsea Sea-Dweller 136660 Stainless Steel Black Dial (2023)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Deepsea Sea-Dweller stands as the ultimate expression of Rolex's professional dive heritage, distilling decades of underwater engineering into a single reference engineered to withstand 3,900 meters — nearly 13,000 feet — of pressure. This legacy traces to the Deep Sea Special that accompanied Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh to the bottom of the Mariana Trench aboard the Trieste in 1960, and was extended in 2012 when James Cameron reached the same depth wearing an experimental Deepsea Challenge. Reference 126660 represents the second-generation Deepsea produced from 2018 through 2023, introducing the Caliber 3235 movement before being superseded by the current 136660. Its patented Ringlock System, helium escape valve, and thick domed sapphire crystal remain among the most impressive engineering statements ever assembled within a wristwatch.

 The 44mm Oyster case in stainless steel employs the patented Ringlock System — an inner nitrogen-alloyed steel compression ring, reinforced caseback, and 5.5mm-thick domed sapphire — alongside a helium escape valve and unidirectional rotatable Cerachrom bezel with platinum-coated numerals. The black dial carries Chromalight luminescent hour markers and Mercedes-style hands for extreme legibility at depth. The in-house automatic Caliber 3235 — equipped with the Chronergy escapement and paramagnetic blue Parachrom hairspring — delivers a 70-hour power reserve and Superlative Chronometer certification, completed by a stainless steel Oyster bracelet with Oysterlock, Glidelock, and Fliplock extension systems.

 Cast in white gold, the case traces the Ellipse's signature rounded silhouette in a slim profile that slips beneath a cuff. The Royal Oak Double Balance Wheel Openworked represents a halo model within Audemars Piguet's catalog, marrying Gérald Genta's 1972 design with one of the brand's most consequential mechanical patents. The double balance system — two mirrored balance wheels and hairsprings stacked on a single axis — enhances stability and precision by averaging out the oscillations of both regulators. Introduced in 2016 in 41mm and subsequently in 37mm with frosted or gem-set executions, the model arrived in 2024 in the classic brushed-and-polished gold finish in this smaller size for the first time, giving collectors a more traditional finishing pairing with the patented caliber that had previously been reserved for the larger or jeweled variants.

 The 37mm case in 18-karat rose gold measures 10mm thick, satin-brushed with polished bevels and the signature octagonal bezel. The openworked rhodium-toned dial reveals the movement's architecture beneath rose gold applied hour markers and luminescent Royal Oak hands, with the patented double balance mechanism visible at eight o'clock. The self-winding in-house Caliber 3132, comprising 245 components and 38 jewels, delivers a 45-hour power reserve and is visible through the sapphire caseback. An integrated rose gold Royal Oak bracelet with AP folding clasp completes the watch.

The 222 occupies a foundational position in Vacheron Constantin's history — launched in 1977 for the 222nd anniversary of the maison's 1755 founding, designed by twenty-four-year-old Jörg Hysek to compete in the emerging luxury steel sports watch category alongside the Royal Oak and Nautilus. The 222 stands as one of the "Holy Three" watches that elevated steel sports watches to icon status, distinguished by its fluted bezel, clean untextured dial, and signature Maltese cross logo positioned at five o'clock on the case rather than the dial. The 222 was discontinued in 1985, and Vacheron Constantin's 2022 revival within the Historiques collection has driven renewed collector interest in original examples — particularly rare precious-metal variants like white gold, which was produced in negligible quantities.

 Measuring a petite 24.4mm in 18-karat white gold, the case features the signature stylized fluted bezel factory-set with brilliant-cut diamonds, alongside the Maltese cross logo at five o'clock and integrated white gold multi-link bracelet flowing seamlessly from case to clasp. The clean dial carries applied hour markers and matching hands beneath a sapphire crystal, framed by the diamond-set bezel that transforms the sport-luxury 222 architecture into a genuine jewelry statement. A precision quartz movement drives the timekeeping, completing one of the rarest material expressions of the model that helped define the luxury sports watch category.

The Patek Philippe Nautilus 7118/1200R-001 represents Patek Philippe's luxurious interpretation of the iconic Nautilus collection designed by Gérald Genta in 1976, scaled to 35.2mm to suit feminine wrists while maintaining the distinctive porthole-inspired octagonal bezel and horizontally embossed dial pattern that has defined the collection for nearly five decades. This reference elevates the sporty elegance characteristic of the Nautilus through factory-set diamond bezel totaling significant carat weight and rose gold case construction, creating a timepiece that transitions seamlessly from casual to formal occasions while maintaining the water resistance and robust build quality expected from one of the most coveted collections in haute horlogologie. The combination of rose gold warmth with silvery-white dial creates sophisticated color harmony, appealing to collectors who value both the revolutionary integrated bracelet sports watch design that challenged watchmaking conventions in the 1970s and the refined femininity achieved through precious materials and gem-setting craftsmanship combined with current-production availability.

 The 35.2mm case crafted in 18-karat rose gold features the signature Nautilus octagonal bezel set with approximately 46 brilliant-cut diamonds, polished surfaces on bezel top and case flanks contrasting with brushed case band, characteristic hinged lugs integrated seamlessly into bracelet design, sapphire crystal, and transparent sapphire caseback revealing the decorated movement. The silvery-white dial displays applied luminous rose gold baton hour markers at all positions except 3 o'clock where the date window resides, polished rose gold baton hands with luminous fill, horizontal embossed pattern characteristic of Nautilus dials creating subtle texture and light play across the surface, black printed minute track along outer edge, and date display at 3 o'clock with white background matching the overall aesthetic. Inside beats the self-winding Caliber 324 S C featuring central rotor in 21-karat gold, 29 jewels, Gyromax balance wheel, Spiromax balance spring in Silinvar silicon, frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour, Patek Philippe Seal certification guaranteeing exceptional finishing and precision standards of minus three to plus two seconds per day, approximately 35 to 45 hours of power reserve. items.model: Audemars Piguet Cobra Vintage White Gold Silver Diamond Dial
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Cobra occupies a remarkable and underrecognized position in Audemars Piguet's history — designed by Gérald Genta in 1971, a full year before he conceived the Royal Oak, and described by the legendary designer himself as his "perfect integration" of case and bracelet. Its extraordinary bracelet, composed of woven 18-karat gold rope-like strands flowing seamlessly from case to clasp, was crafted by GRG — the renowned Swiss jeweler Roland Gilbert Gaschen — whom Audemars Piguet entrusted with its most intricate precious-metal bracelet work throughout the 1970s. Vintage Cobras in white gold rank among the rarest material expressions of the reference, as the collection was produced in far fewer numbers than the Royal Oak that followed, with white gold executions constituting only a fraction of the already limited yellow gold production.

 The 29 x 32mm cushion-shaped case in 18-karat white gold flows seamlessly into the signature integrated Polonaise mesh bracelet, whose woven ten-strand construction creates the serpentine scale-like surface that inspired the Cobra nickname. The silver dial carries diamond hour markers and the applied AP logo at twelve beneath slender white gold hands, uncluttered by additional complications and allowing the interplay of white gold, silver, and diamonds to define the composition. A precision movement drives the timekeeping, completing one of the most historically significant vintage Audemars Piguet references within Genta's early design canon and representing an especially rare petite ladies' expression of his integrated bracelet philosophy.

items.model: Vacheron Constantin Overseas 4300V/120R-B547 Perpetual Calendar Ultra-Thin Skeleton Rose Gold
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Overseas Perpetual Calendar Ultra-Thin Skeleton distills three of Vacheron Constantin's most consequential horological achievements — the perpetual calendar, ultra-thin construction, and complete openworking — into a single contemporary reference within the maison's traveler-oriented flagship line. Reference 4300V/120R-B547 executes this ambitious trinity in 18-karat 5N pink gold with striking blue accents throughout the skeletonized dial architecture. Vacheron Constantin's standing as the oldest continuously operating watch manufacture in the world — founded 1755 — combined with the movement's Hallmark of Geneva certification places this reference among the most pedigreed contemporary sports complications available. The result transforms the Overseas from a sport-luxury tool into a wearable manifestation of haute horlogerie, presenting the maison's most technically ambitious calibre through an entirely revealed movement.

 The 41.5mm case in 18-karat 5N pink gold measures just 8.1mm thick, framed by the signature six-sided notched Maltese cross-inspired bezel and transparent sapphire caseback. The fully openworked dial reveals the movement architecture in its entirety, with blue accents distinguishing the printed markers, hands, day, date, month, leap year indications, and moon phase at six. The in-house automatic Caliber 1120 QPSQ/1 — 276 components at just 4.05mm thick with 22-karat gold NAC-treated openworked oscillating weight — delivers 40 hours of reserve, completed by Vacheron's patented quick-release system with pink gold half-Maltese-cross bracelet, blue calfskin, and blue rubber straps.

items.model: Rolex Daytona 6262 'Blue' Stainless Steel Black 'Reverse Panda' Dial (1970)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The reference 6262 occupies one of the most coveted positions in vintage Rolex Daytona collecting — produced for only a single year in 1970 as a transitional reference bridging the early and late manual-winding Daytonas, and consequently ranking among the rarest Daytonas ever made. This particular execution carries the additional distinction of a "Blue" Daytona dial — the coveted natural patina phenomenon where the printed "DAYTONA" text above the six o'clock register has aged from white silver print into a soft baby blue tone, a change that occurs organically over decades on select Singer-made vintage dials. The combination of the reference's transitional rarity with the Blue Daytona patina places this example among the most coveted vintage Daytonas in the collector market today.

 The 37mm case in stainless steel features pump chronograph pushers, screw-down crown, and stainless steel tachymetric bezel engraved to 200 mph. The matte black dial carries three silver subdials — running seconds at nine, 30-minute counter at three, 12-hour counter at six — with tritium lume plots and the signature "DAYTONA" text patinated to soft blue above the six o'clock register. The manual-winding Valjoux Caliber 727 — a nickel-finished lever movement at 21,600 vibrations per hour — represented an evolution beyond the earlier 722 caliber, completed by a vintage stainless steel Rolex Oyster bracelet.

 The 40mm case in 18-karat Everose gold features the factory rainbow sapphire bezel and Triplock screw-down crown with matching chronograph pushers, alongside factory brilliant-cut diamonds set into the lugs and crown guards. The diamond-paved dial carries baguette-cut sapphire hour markers matched to the bezel's rainbow gradient, three Everose gold subdials for chronograph functions, and matching Everose gold hands. The in-house automatic Caliber 4131 — a self-winding chronograph with column wheel and vertical clutch — delivers a 72-hour power reserve and Superlative Chronometer certification, completed by an 18-karat Everose gold Oyster bracelet with Oysterlock folding safety clasp.

The Vagabondage II ranks among F.P.Journe's rarest and most horologically ambitious creations — the second installment in the celebrated Vagabondage trilogy that ran from 2004 through 2017, and limited here to just 68 examples in 18-karat 6N rose gold. Introduced in 2010, this reference marked a landmark technical achievement as the first F.P.Journe wristwatch to combine both digital jumping hours and digital jumping minutes, requiring the development of a specific barrel and a remontoir d'égalité constant-force mechanism to power the instantaneous jumps without disturbing timekeeping precision. Owners of the original Vagabondage I received priority to acquire matching serial numbers, reinforcing the exclusivity of this series within the collector community and cementing the Vagabondage's status as one of independent watchmaking's most cerebral productions.

 The Flat Tortue-shaped case in 18-karat rose gold measures 45.2 x 37.5mm and stands just 8mm thick, framing a smoked sapphire dial deliberately free of the F.P.Journe signature — a Vagabondage tradition — that reveals the 18-karat rose gold movement beneath. Digital jumping hour and minute apertures dominate the center, complemented by analog small seconds at six and power reserve indication at twelve. The hand-wound Caliber 1509 with remontoir d'égalité delivers approximately 40 hours of reserve, completed by an alligator strap with 18-karat rose gold folding clasp.

 *This is a limited edition of 68 pieces.

Named for 1815 — the birth year of Ferdinand Adolph Lange, founder of A. Lange & Söhne and pioneer of German watchmaking whose development of the Glashütte lever escapement transformed the Saxon town into Germany's watchmaking capital — the 1815 collection channels his nineteenth-century pocket-watch heritage through Arabic numerals, blued steel hands, and railway-style minute tracks. Reference 234.021 represents the current-generation 1815 Up/Down in 18-karat yellow gold, introduced in 2013 as a comprehensively updated evolution of the original 221.021 that ran from 1997 to 2008. The "Up/Down" designation refers to the "AUF/AB" power reserve indicator drawn from traditional German pocket watch terminology, one of Lange's most distinctively characterful complications and a nod to the maison's Saxon horological roots.

 The 39mm case in 18-karat yellow gold measures just 8.7mm thick and presents a solid silver argenté dial with black Arabic numerals, small seconds asymmetrically placed at four, power reserve indicator at eight marked AUF/AB, a railway-style minute track, and blued steel hands. The hand-wound Caliber L051.2 — 245 components featuring the three-quarter plate in untreated German silver, screwed gold chatons, and hand-engraved balance cock that define Lange's finishing tradition — delivers a 72-hour power reserve visible through the sapphire caseback, completed by a hand-stitched crocodile leather strap with 18-karat yellow gold pin buckle.

The Royal Oak Offshore debuted in 1993 with reference 25721ST — designed by Emmanuel Gueit and famously nicknamed "The Beast" by Gérald Genta himself. The reference established an entirely new genre of oversized luxury sport chronographs that has influenced the watchmaking industry ever since. Released in November 2021, reference 26238ST represents the modernized reissue of the original as part of the permanent collection — succeeding the 2018 25th-anniversary limited edition — and faithfully reproduces the 1993 dial architecture with the "Petite Tapisserie" pattern and original 12-9-6 subdial layout. It also introduced the manufacture's new in-house Caliber 4404 — the first integrated flyback chronograph developed specifically for the Offshore line.

 The 42mm case in stainless steel measures 14.4mm thick, framed by the signature octagonal bezel with eight hexagonal screws, blue rubber-clad pushers and screw-locked crown, and sapphire caseback replacing the original 1993 solid back. The blue "Petite Tapisserie" dial carries blue chronograph counters, white gold applied hour markers and Royal Oak hands with luminescent coating, blue inner bezel, and date at three. The in-house automatic Caliber 4404 — 433 components with column wheel and vertical clutch — delivers a 70-hour power reserve, completed by the stainless steel Royal Oak Offshore bracelet with an additional blue rubber strap via interchangeable system.

items.sourceDescription:
Launched in 2016, the Royal Oak Double Balance Wheel openworked introduced one of Audemars Piguet's most significant mechanical innovations of the modern era. The patented double balance wheel system positions two balance wheels and two hairsprings on the same axis, oscillating in harmony to counteract positional errors and enhance chronometric stability — a genuinely novel departure from centuries of single-balance wheel construction. Reference 15407ST executes this innovation within the iconic 41mm Royal Oak silhouette in stainless steel, distinguished by an openworked dial revealing the entirety of the Caliber 3132 architecture. The visual language combines gunmetal grey bridges with pink gold accents on the applied hour markers and balance bridge, creating a contemporary two-tone aesthetic that has secured this reference's place among the most coveted openworked Royal Oaks in production.

 The 41mm case in stainless steel measures just 9.9mm thick, featuring the signature octagonal bezel with eight hexagonal screws, screw-locked crown, and glareproofed sapphire crystal and caseback. The slate grey openworked dial reveals the movement architecture with pink gold applied hour markers and Royal Oak hands with luminescent coating. The in-house self-winding Caliber 3132 — 245 components at just 5.57mm thick with the patented double balance wheel mechanism — delivers a 45-hour power reserve, hand-finished throughout with beveled bridges and polished surfaces, completed by an integrated stainless steel Royal Oak bracelet with AP folding clasp.

The Overseas occupies an essential place in the history of the luxury sports watch, with design lineage tracing to the 1977 Vacheron Constantin 222 — the maison's 222nd-anniversary creation that stood alongside the Royal Oak and Nautilus as one of the era's defining integrated sports watches. Reference 4520V/210R-B967 debuted in 2024 as the self-winding rose gold expression paired with an intense sunburst green dial, the most restrained of the trio that also comprises green-dial Chronograph and Dual Time variants. Vacheron Constantin's standing as the oldest continuously operating watch manufacture in the world — founded 1755 — combined with the movement's Geneva Hallmark certification places this reference among the most pedigreed contemporary luxury sports watches in production.

 The 41mm case in 18-karat 5N pink gold measures 10.69mm thick, framed by the signature six-sided notched bezel inspired by the Maltese cross. The green sunburst dial with translucent lacquered finish and velvet-finished flange creates layered depth, complemented by 18-karat gold applied hour markers and dagger-style hands with blue SuperLuminova, alongside a date aperture at three. The in-house automatic Caliber 5100 — visible through the sapphire caseback via its 22-karat gold wind-rose-inspired rotor — delivers a 60-hour power reserve and carries the Geneva Hallmark, completed by Vacheron's quick-release system with three interchangeable straps: pink gold bracelet, green calfskin leather, and green rubber.

 *This timepiece comes with a rose gold bracelet, rubber strap, leather strap, and the original hang tag.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Lange 1 stands as A. Lange & Söhne's most iconic modern reference — announced October 24, 1994 as one of the four foundational watches following the brand's revival after decades of dormancy imposed by East German communist expropriation. Its asymmetric off-center dial layout was revolutionary, and the outsized date display was the first in modern watchmaking history. The Lange 1 Time Zone debuted in 2005 as the traveler's iteration, and reference 136.029 represents the third-generation update released in 2020 — the first movement change to the Time Zone in fifteen years, powered by the new in-house Caliber L141.1. Configured in white gold with a black solid silver dial, this remains one of the most sophisticated dual-time wristwatches ever produced.

 The 41.9mm case in 18-karat white gold measures 10.9mm thick, framing the black solid silver dial with applied white gold hour markers. The signature layout displays home time with Roman numerals at upper left, second time zone at five with Arabic numerals, outsize date at twelve, small seconds, power reserve indicator, and a rotating city ring for 24 reference cities operated by the pusher at eight. The hand-wound Caliber L141.1 — 448 parts with three-quarter plate in untreated German silver and hand-engraved balance cock — delivers a 72-hour power reserve, completed by a hand-stitched black alligator strap with white gold pin buckle.

Released in February 2026 as the inaugural model of the new Neo Frame collection — which replaces the [Re]master series as Audemars Piguet's vintage-inspired reissue line — this rectangular timepiece draws direct inspiration from AP's Pre-Model 1271 of 1929, a rare Streamline Moderne jumping hour produced only in 1929 and 1930. Between 1924 and 1951, Audemars Piguet sold 347 timepieces with the jumping hour complication, but this reference marks a genuine horological first for the manufacture: the debut of Calibre 7122, Audemars Piguet's first-ever self-winding jumping hour movement. It represents the maison's boldest departure from the Royal Oak-dominated catalog in years, quietly celebrated by collectors seeking AP's more archival, form-driven side.

 The 34 x 34mm rectangular case in 18-karat pink gold measures just 8.8mm thick and features the signature eight vertical gadroons on each side extending onto the lugs — the Streamline detail preserved from the 1929 original. The black PVD-treated sapphire dial — bonded directly to the sapphire and screwed into the case — displays the jumping hour at twelve and trailing minutes at six through pink gold-toned microblasted apertures. The self-winding Caliber 7122, with titanium hour disc and patented shock-absorbing system, delivers a 52-hour power reserve, completed by an integrated textured black calfskin leather strap with pink gold pin buckle.

items.model: Breguet Tradition Tourbillon 7047PT/1Y/9ZU Platinum Blue Dial (2023)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Abraham-Louis Breguet occupies unrivaled status as the most influential watchmaker in history — inventor of the tourbillon in 1801, the Breguet balance spring, the perpetual calendar mechanism, and countless other foundational contributions to horology. The Tradition collection, launched in 2005, uniquely inverts the movement to display Breguet's most celebrated mechanisms on the dial side, drawing inspiration from the souscription pocket watches he sold by advance subscription in the 1790s. Reference 7047 unites two of his most consequential inventions: the tourbillon and the fusée-and-chain transmission, a constant-force mechanism where a fine 232-link chain unwinds from the mainspring barrel onto a cone-shaped fusée pulley, ensuring consistent torque to the escapement regardless of state of wind.

 The 41mm case in platinum measures 15.95mm thick, distinguished by the signature fluted caseband, individually welded lugs with screw pins, and ultra-domed sapphire crystal. The off-centered blue hand-guilloché gold sub-dial at seven carries the traditional "Clous de Paris" pattern, Roman numerals, individual serial number, and Breguet pomme hands. The visible Caliber 569 — a 542-component hand-wound movement with fusée-and-chain transmission and one-minute tourbillon with titanium cage and silicon balance spring — delivers 50 hours of reserve, completed by a midnight blue alligator strap with triple-blade platinum folding clasp.

 *This timepiece has factory stickers on the case.

The 5160G-001 stands among the rarest modern Patek Philippe productions — announced at BaselWorld 2010 as part of the maison's Rare Handcrafts collection and  Grand Complications collection, with roughly twenty examples (although no number was ever published by Patek) believed to have been produced in 18-karat white gold before its discontinuation. Rare Handcrafts represents Patek Philippe's designation for pieces incorporating traditional artistic crafts practiced at the highest artisanal level, preserving techniques that would otherwise disappear. Every visible surface of the officer's-style case — bezel, lugs, sides, crown, buckle, and hinged caseback — is entirely hand-engraved with foliate and volute motifs inspired by a pocket watch in the Patek Philippe Museum, transforming this perpetual calendar into a genuine work of métiers d'art.

 The 38mm officer's-style case in 18-karat white gold features the entirely hand-engraved surfaces including a hinged dust cover concealing the sapphire display back. The silvery opaline dial carries a hand-engraved foliate center, black Roman numeral hours, a red-tipped retrograde date pointer sweeping across an arc of alternating Arabic numerals, apertures for day at nine, leap year at twelve, and month at three, and a moon phase at six. The self-winding Caliber 324 S QR — a perpetual calendar with retrograde date — delivers 45 hours of reserve and requires no correction until 2100, completed by a black alligator strap with hand-engraved white gold fold-over clasp.

 *This timepiece comes with a stylus.

Reference 5170P-001 arrived in 2017 as the platinum flagship of this line, produced for only approximately one year before its 2018 discontinuation — a remarkably brief production window that has secured the reference significant collectible status. The platinum case is identified by the signature diamond set into the case flank at six o'clock, one of Patek's most subtle luxury markers, quietly identifying platinum to those familiar with the code.

 The 39.4mm case in platinum features the sapphire display caseback revealing the movement and Patek Philippe's characteristic identifying diamond at six. The blue sunburst dial gradates to black at the edges — the signature fumé effect — with nine applied baguette-cut diamond hour markers appearing almost as polished metal batons, a central chronograph seconds hand, thirty-minute counter at three, and small subsidiary seconds at nine. The hand-wound Caliber CH 29-535 PS — a 269-part chronograph with instantaneously jumping minutes and column wheel construction — delivers 65 hours of power reserve and carries the Patek Philippe Seal, completed by a black alligator strap with platinum fold-over clasp.

The Panthère de Cartier is the house's most enduring integrated bracelet watch design — introduced in 1983 and continuously coveted across four decades for its sinuous three-row bracelet architecture and the seamless way case and bracelet merge into a single fluid form. The midsize at 27mm occupies the most versatile position in the Panthère's size hierarchy: substantial enough to register with clear presence on the wrist, refined enough to function as jewellery in contexts where the larger configuration would be excessive. The diamond-set bezel variant elevates this particular example into explicitly high jewellery territory, while the date complication — visible at three o'clock — confirms this as a watches-and-jewellery proposition rather than a purely decorative object. Vintage yellow gold Panthères with diamond bezels and three-row bracelets command sustained collector attention for both their design integrity and their material quality.

 The 27mm yellow gold cushion-form case carries a single-row diamond-set bezel, with the characteristic three-row articulated yellow gold bracelet flowing directly from the case flanks. The cream dial presents bold black Roman numerals, a fine inner railroad minute chapter, and a date aperture at three o'clock. Blued-steel sword hands and a gold sapphire cabochon crown complete the dial. A Swiss quartz movement powers the watch.

items.model: F.P. Journe Octa Réserve de Marche Ref. A Platinum White Gold Dial Brass Movement 'Souscription' Limited Edition of 20 (2003)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
This example belongs to one of the most historically consequential series ever produced by F.P.Journe. The Souscription program traces to 1999, when twenty close clients and friends committed deposits that allowed the fledgling manufacture to survive and flourish — a founding gesture that shaped modern independent watchmaking. Those same twenty clients received the exclusive right to acquire the first twenty  Octa Réserve de Marche pieces, cementing their status as F.P.Journe's founding patrons. Released in 2001 as Journe's third creation under his own name, the Octa marked the world's first automatic movement to deliver 120 hours of chronometric precision. The rhodium-plated brass movement — produced only until 2004 across roughly 2,000 pieces total — makes this among the most coveted early Journe configurations.

 The 38mm platinum case measures 10.6mm thick and houses a raw uncoated 18-karat white gold dial with grainy matte finish paired with whitened guilloché silver subdials. The signature asymmetric layout displays off-center hours and minutes, small seconds at four-thirty, a large date at twelve, and a power reserve indicator arcing from zero to 120 hours at seven-thirty. The bi-directional automatic Caliber 1300 in rhodium-plated brass — with 22-karat gold off-center rotor and free-sprung balance — delivers five days of power reserve, completed by the original burlwood presentation box and blue-grey suede strap.

 *This is a limited edition of 20 pieces reserved for owners of original Tourbillon Souverain.

items.model: Patek Philippe Grand Complications 5236P-001 In-Line Perpetual Calendar Platinum Blue Dial (2022)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The 5236P-001 introduced one of the most significant perpetual calendar developments in modern watchmaking. Unveiled at Watches & Wonders 2021, it became the first wristwatch perpetual calendar to display day, date, and month in a single horizontal aperture at twelve — a configuration historically reserved for rare pocket watches and protected here by three pending patents. For collectors of Patek's  Grand Complications , the reference represents a rare instance of genuine mechanical innovation rather than refinement, while the case design draws lineage from the legendary 3448, the maison's first automatic perpetual calendar from 1962.

 The 41.3mm platinum case measures 11.07mm thick and frames a blue dial with black-gradient rim and vertical satin finish, accented by faceted white gold baton hour markers and the in-line calendar aperture at twelve. Moon phase and small seconds occupy six o'clock, with leap year and day/night indications in subsidiary apertures. The self-winding Caliber 31-260 PS QL — built from 503 components and incorporating an off-center platinum mini-rotor — delivers up to 48 hours of reserve. A signature platinum diamond between the lugs at six and a navy alligator strap with platinum fold-over clasp complete the piece.

Reference 116576TBR represents the diamond-set escalation of the first-ever platinum Daytona — introduced in 2013 to mark the model's 50th anniversary — and occupies rarefied territory as one of the maison's most prestigious modern productions. The ice blue dial itself remains reserved exclusively for platinum Rolex watches, functioning as an instantly recognizable identifier of the material from across a room. Executed here with a clean ice blue sunburst dial punctuated by factory baguette-cut diamond hour markers rather than full pavé treatment, this configuration achieves a more restrained yet still magnificent expression of the reference.

 The 40mm case in 950 platinum features a bezel factory-set with thirty-six diamonds and Triplock screw-down crown with matching chronograph pushers. The ice blue sunburst dial carries baguette-cut diamond hour markers, three tonal ice blue subdials — small seconds at six, thirty-minute counter at three, twelve-hour counter at nine — the signature red "Daytona" text above six, and blued white gold hands. The in-house automatic Caliber 4130 — a self-winding chronograph with column wheel and vertical clutch — delivers a 72-hour power reserve and Superlative Chronometer certification, completed by a 950 platinum Oyster bracelet with Oysterlock folding safety clasp.

The smoked taupe variant (reference 26420SO.OO.A600CA.01) offers a sophisticated color treatment rarely seen in sports chronographs, with graduated tones transitioning from light brown at the center to darker edges across the signature Méga Tapisserie pattern. The 26420 also introduces refined subdial positioning and updated proportions compared to earlier 42mm Offshore chronographs, creating better visual balance while maintaining the collection's bold, muscular presence established since the Offshore's 1993 debut.

 The 43mm stainless steel case measures 14.4mm thick with octagonal architecture secured by eight hexagonal screws across the black ceramic bezel. Sandblasted stainless steel pushpiece guards flank the black ceramic chronograph pushers and screw-locked crown. Glareproofed sapphire crystals protect both dial and exhibition caseback. The smoked light brown dial showcases the new-generation Méga Tapisserie waffle pattern with black chronograph counters at 3, 6, and 9 o'clock positioned against black outer zone. White gold applied hour markers and Royal Oak hands feature luminescent coating. Black inner bezel displays tachymeter scale, date window positioned at 4:30. Manufacture Caliber 4401 automatic integrated chronograph features column-wheel mechanism with flyback function, operating at 28,800 vph with 40 jewels, 367 components, and 70-hour power reserve.

Genta himself described the Cobra as "magnificent," particularly admiring the seamless integration between case and bracelet. Famously worn by the last Shah of Iran, the model remained more exclusive than the Royal Oak that followed, today appreciated by collectors who value its serpentine bracelet — a Polonaise mesh whose scale-like weave inspired the "Cobra" nickname — as one of the most distinctive integrated bracelets in vintage watchmaking.

 The 30mm cushion-shaped case in 18-karat yellow gold features the signature integrated Polonaise mesh bracelet with its braided, scale-like surface flowing seamlessly from case to clasp. The champagne dial carries eight diamond hour markers, the applied AP logo at twelve, and diamond-set sword-shaped hands — an unusually opulent jewelry detail rarely seen on hands themselves. A precision movement drives the timekeeping, completed by the seamlessly integrated yellow gold Polonaise mesh bracelet that has made the Cobra one of the most distinctive expressions of vintage Genta design.

 *This example was produced in the 1980s, and sold in 1999 (on the original paper).

Greubel Forsey occupies a singular place in contemporary haute horlogerie as one of the most uncompromising independents — founded by Robert Greubel and Stephen Forsey in 2004 and renowned for inventions like the Quadruple Tourbillon, the Double Tourbillon 30°, and a standard of 100% hand-finishing rarely matched at any price. The Balancier 3, introduced in late 2023 and produced from 2024 through 2028, represents the atelier's most accessible entry into its world — limited to just 88 pieces per colorway, the result of nearly twenty years of consideration. It distills the brand's full technical and finishing language into a more direct, sports-oriented expression, characterized by three architecturally suspended bridges and a 12.6mm variable-inertia balance wheel — among the largest in contemporary watchmaking.

 The 41.5mm Convexe case in titanium measures 13.35mm thick, the lugs unscrewed for the first time in Greubel Forsey's history and profiled to follow the wrist's natural curvature. The openworked black dial displays the balance wheel at five, fast-rotating barrels at one and ten, small seconds at eight beneath a fixed red triangle, and an arch bridge carrying the hour and minute hands. The hand-wound in-house caliber comprises 282 parts and 43 jewels seated in olived gold chatons, delivering a 72-hour chronometric reserve via twin coupled barrels, completed by a rubber strap with titanium folding clasp.

 *This is a limited edition of 88 pieces.

 *The retail price of this watch is $228,000.

The Rolex Day-Date  occupies an unmatched position as Rolex's flagship statement piece, executed exclusively in precious metals since its 1956 introduction. Reference 228236 represents the platinum execution of the modern 40mm generation, distinguished by a fluted platinum bezel — a configuration of particular consequence, as fluted bezels in platinum remain among the less commonly produced variants of the line. Paired with the meteorite dial, this reference draws collectors seeking the convergence of Rolex's most precious metal with one of its rarest dial materials, each example bearing a Widmanstätten crystalline pattern that cannot be replicated between watches.

 The 40mm case in 950 platinum carries a fluted platinum bezel and frames a meteorite dial set with ten baguette-cut diamond hour markers. The day aperture sits at twelve, with the date at three beneath the Cyclops magnifier. Inside, the in-house Caliber 3255 — featuring the Chronergy escapement and Parachrom hairspring — delivers a 70-hour power reserve. The watch is completed by a solid platinum President bracelet with semi-circular three-piece links and concealed folding Crownclasp.

 *This timepiece comes with the original white hang tag.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Patek Philippe Nautilus  arrived in 1976 as Gérald Genta's vision of an elegant luxury sports watch — defined by its rounded octagonal "porthole" bezel and integrated bracelet, securing its place alongside the Royal Oak as a foundational reference in modern watchmaking. The 7010 series represents Patek Philippe's contemporary ladies' interpretation, scaling the model's proportions to a more refined 32mm while introducing the signature diamond-set bezel and gem-jewelry elegance that distinguishes the women's collection. Configured here in 18-karat white gold with a silver dial, the reference offers the most discreet and sophisticated execution of the ladies' Nautilus — a precious-metal sports watch that moves comfortably between formal and everyday wear.

 The 32mm case in 18-karat white gold measures just 6.9mm thick, framed by the signature rounded octagonal bezel set with 46 brilliant-cut diamonds totaling approximately 0.8 carats, with alternating polished and satin finishes. The silver dial bears the Nautilus's signature horizontal "wave" embossing, with applied white gold hour markers and luminescent coating, alpha-style hands, and date at three. The precision quartz Caliber E23-250 S C drives the timekeeping with exceptional accuracy, completed by a white leather strap with white gold Nautilus fold-over clasp.

items.model: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak 77452BC.ZZ.1365BC.01 White Gold Snow-Set Brilliant Cut Full Diamond Pave
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
This reference marks a significant high-jewelry milestone for Audemars Piguet : the first time the maison applied the snow-set gem-setting technique to the Royal Oak . Released in 2023, the snow setting represents one of the most demanding methods in haute joaillerie, employing diamonds of varying sizes arranged in an irregular yet cohesive mosaic — like snowflakes blanketing a surface — to produce a textured visual depth that uniformly paved gem-setting cannot achieve. With over 2,250 diamonds totaling nearly seven carats covering case, bezel, dial, crown, and integrated bracelet, the reference unites Gérald Genta's 1972 architecture with the manufacture's most ambitious contemporary high-jewelry execution, placing it among the rarest expressions of the model.

 The 34mm case in 18-karat white gold measures 9.2mm thick, its octagonal bezel snow-set with brilliant-cut diamonds alongside the signature hexagonal screws, with the crown additionally diamond-set. The 18-karat white gold dial is snow-set with 879 brilliant-cut diamonds and accented by thirteen baguette-cut diamond hour markers, with white gold Royal Oak hands carrying luminescent coating. A self-winding movement powers the hours, minutes, and center seconds, completed by an integrated white gold Royal Oak bracelet snow-set with 1,100 brilliant-cut diamonds and AP folding clasp.

items.sourceDescription:
Unveiled at Watches & Wonders 2026, the green ombré Datejust represents one of the most anticipated dial releases Rolex has produced in years — the first ombré execution the manufacture has rendered entirely in lacquer. Green has long held particular significance for Rolex, the color invoked for anniversary models including the GMT-Master II 50th and Submariner 50th, and its application to one of watchmaking's most foundational references — the original 1945 Datejust, the first self-winding waterproof chronometer to display the date — has generated immediate collector enthusiasm. Reference 126200 stands as the most quietly refined of the green ombré variants, the stainless steel-on-Oyster execution that lets the dial speak as the singular focus.

 The 36mm Oystersteel case carries a smooth domed bezel and Twinlock screw-down crown. The green lacquer dial is created through a process unique to this generation — green lacquer applied to the base plate, then black lacquer sprayed in concentric motions toward the edges to produce a gradient transitioning from vivid green at the center to shadowy near-black at the perimeter, accented by white gold baton markers with Chromalight luminescence. The in-house automatic Caliber 3235 delivers a 70-hour power reserve, completed by an Oystersteel Oyster bracelet with Oysterclasp and Easylink extension.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Chronographe FB carries singular significance in F.P.Journe's modern history as the final limited series the manufacture will ever produce. Released in 2024 to commemorate the twentieth anniversary of the Tokyo Boutique — opened September 2003 in the Omotesando district and the first time an independent watchmaker established a boutique under his own name, marking the starting point of F.P.Journe's global expansion — it represents the sixth and concluding chapter of the Tokyo Boutique Anniversaire Series. Limited to just 200 pieces and announced as the last numbered, fixed-batch edition the brand will ever create, the reference closes a defining era of independent watchmaking collector culture built on allocation and insider access.

 The 40mm polished titanium case measures 10.4mm thick, paired with 18-karat 6N rose gold crown and flyback chronograph pushers. The ruthenium-coated guilloché silver dial features sapphire subdials, rose gold Arabic numerals, central flyback chronograph seconds completing one rotation per two minutes, sixty-minute counter at three, sixty-second counter at nine, and a big date at six. The new in-house Caliber 1518.2 — a hand-wound flyback chronograph with column wheel in 18-karat rose gold — delivers an 80-hour power reserve, completed by a burgundy alligator strap with 18-karat rose gold folding clasp.

 *This is a limited edition of 200 pieces, and this is the last limited edition F.P.Journe ever made.

The Sky-Dweller stands as the most complicated watch Rolex has ever produced and the only model in the catalog to feature an annual calendar, automatically distinguishing between thirty- and thirty-one-day months while requiring correction only once a year. Reference 326259TBR represents the gem-set Sky-Dweller paired with the contemporary Oysterflex bracelet — Rolex's high-performance elastomer compound molded over a titanium and nickel blade — for a configuration that pairs maximum opulence with sport-luxury wearability. The 42mm white gold case is set with a factory baguette-cut diamond bezel, brilliant-cut diamonds across case sides and lugs, while the meteorite dial — sliced from an extraterrestrial iron meteorite with its unique Widmanstätten crystalline pattern — places this reference among the rarest gem-set Rolex creations.

 The 42mm case in 18-karat white gold features a bezel set with baguette-cut diamonds and brilliant-cut diamonds across the case sides and lugs. The meteorite dial carries ten baguette-cut diamond hour markers, an off-center 24-hour disc displaying the second time zone, date at three beneath the Cyclops, and month indication through twelve apertures around the circumference, governed by the fluted Ring Command bezel. The automatic Caliber 9001 delivers a 72-hour power reserve, completed by a black Oysterflex bracelet with white gold Oysterclasp.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Speedmaster Professional holds singular status in watchmaking history as the only timepiece worn during all six Apollo Moon landings — certified by NASA in 1965 for all manned space missions following rigorous testing against extreme temperature, pressure, vibration, and acceleration. It remains qualified for NASA spaceflight to this day. Reference 310.30.42.50.01.001 represents the current "hesalite" execution introduced in 2021 alongside the new Calibre 3861, faithfully preserving the original Moonwatch specifications: the hesalite plexiglass crystal that won't shatter in vacuum, and the solid steel caseback bearing the embossed Seahorse medallion — the configuration that NASA originally approved for orbital and lunar use.

 The 42mm asymmetrical case in stainless steel measures 13.18mm thick, framed by a black anodized aluminum bezel bearing the tachymeter scale and the famous "dot over 90" detail. The matte black step dial features applied Omega logo, printed luminescent hour markers, and a tri-compax chronograph layout with small seconds at nine, thirty-minute counter at three, and twelve-hour counter at six. The manual-winding Calibre 3861 — Co-Axial Master Chronometer certified by METAS and anti-magnetic to 15,000 gauss — delivers a 50-hour power reserve, completed by a brushed stainless steel five-arched-links bracelet with foldover clasp.

Its understated configuration has made it among the most coveted vintage-era Offshores on the secondary market.

 The 42mm case in stainless steel measures 14.2mm thick, with the signature octagonal bezel secured by eight white gold hexagonal screws and black rubber-clad screw-down crown and pushers. The in-house automatic Caliber 3126/3840 — derived from the Caliber 3120 with a chronograph module — delivers a 50-hour power reserve, completed by the signature brown hornback alligator strap with cream contrast stitching and steel AP folding clasp.

When the 15202 line was retired in 2022 to mark the Royal Oak's fiftieth anniversary, this reference cemented its place among the most coveted of the entire production run.

 The 39mm case measures just 8.1mm thick, executed in grade-5 titanium with a polished 950 platinum bezel framing a smoked blue "Petite Tapisserie" dial. White gold applied hour markers, Royal Oak hands, and the applied AP logo at six accompany a date aperture at three. The legendary Caliber 2121 — descended from the JLC 920 used in the 1972 Royal Oak, just 3.05mm thick with central rotor and 2.75Hz frequency — delivers a 40-hour power reserve, visible through the sapphire caseback. A titanium bracelet with polished platinum center links completes the watch.

The Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 26579CE holds a landmark place in Audemars Piguet's history as the first watch the manufacture produced entirely in ceramic — both case and bracelet — when it debuted at SIHH 2017. The achievement was anything but routine: the Royal Oak's intricately integrated bracelet and faceted octagonal case posed extraordinary challenges in a material six times harder to finish than steel, requiring 600 hours of research and development, with the bracelet finishing alone consuming thirty hours per watch. The result unites Gérald Genta's 1972 design with one of horology's most revered complications in a nearly scratchproof, remarkably light stealth-luxury package that remains among the most coveted modern Royal Oaks.

 The 41mm case in black ceramic measures 9.5mm thick, framing a slate grey "Grande Tapisserie" dial with black counters, white gold applied hour markers, and a black inner bezel bearing the week indicator. The perpetual calendar displays day at nine, date at three, month and leap year at twelve, and astronomical moon phase at six. The ultra-thin self-winding Caliber 5134, derived from the legendary 2120 of the original Royal Oak, delivers a 40-hour power reserve and is visible through the sapphire caseback. A full black ceramic Royal Oak bracelet with titanium folding clasp completes the watch.

*The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 26579CE.OO.1225CE.01 is a discontinued model.

 The 36mm case in 18-karat white gold carries a bezel set with 52 brilliant-cut diamonds, framing a lapis lazuli dial with diamond-set Roman numerals in 18-karat gold settings, day aperture at twelve, and date at three beneath the Cyclops magnifier. The platinum execution on its matching platinum bracelet stands among the scarcest configurations of the line, rarely surfacing on the secondary market.

 The 38mm platinum case measures 10.6mm thick and frames the signature two-tone asymmetric dial in 18-karat white gold and whitened guilloché silver. Blued steel hands accent the composition, completed by an integrated platinum bracelet with deployant clasp.

The A. Lange & Söhne Zeitwerk  stands among the most consequential original creations in twenty-first-century watchmaking. Introduced in 2009, it presented the first mechanical wristwatch with large, precisely jumping digital hours and minutes — a configuration long considered impractical given the energy required to instantaneously advance the discs. Reference 142.025 represents the new-generation Zeitwerk launched in 2022, executed in platinum with the rhodié dial and refined Caliber L043.6 that doubled the original's power reserve. For collectors, it embodies A. Lange & Söhne's willingness to engineer entirely new mechanical solutions rather than refine existing ones, securing its standing as a modern grail among independents and connoisseurs alike.

 The 41.9mm case in 950 platinum measures 12.2mm in height and frames a rhodié solid silver dial bisected by a black-rhodiumed time bridge in German silver. Three apertures display jumping hours at left and jumping minutes at right, with subsidiary seconds beneath and AUF/AB power reserve indicator above. The manual-wind Caliber L043.6 with patented remontoir constant-force mechanism delivers 72 hours of reserve, completed by a dark brown alligator strap with platinum deployant clasp.

Where the Datograph adds an outsized date and the Triple Split layers further complications, the 1815 strips the configuration to its essentials — preserving the dial architecture of Lange's historic pocket chronographs while housing one of the most accomplished manually-wound chronograph movements in modern production. The flyback function and precisely jumping minute counter, defining features of Lange chronographs since 1999, position this reference among the most respected understated chronographs available from any contemporary manufacture.

 The 39.5mm case in 18-karat pink gold measures approximately 11mm thick and frames a solid silver black dial with railway-track minute scale, applied Arabic numerals, and a pulsations scale graduated for 30 pulsations. Twin subdials below center display thirty-minute counter and small seconds. The manual-wind Caliber L951.5, featuring hand-engraved balance cock and untreated German silver three-quarter plate, delivers 60 hours of power reserve, visible through the sapphire caseback. A black alligator strap with pink gold deployant clasp completes the watch.

The 5212A's stainless steel construction — a material Patek Philippe deploys with deliberate selectivity across its Complications range — signals accessibility relative to the precious metal catalogue, a reading reinforced by the tan calfskin strap with cream stitching.

 The 40mm stainless steel case carries a polished bezel and screw-down case back. The silver opaline dial presents three concentric rings: an outer ring carrying week numbers 1–53 interspersed with printed month names; a middle ring displaying the full day name; and an inner opaline field with applied baton hour markers and a date aperture at three o'clock. A red-tipped seconds hand provides the sole colour accent. A calfskin strap with cream stitching and stainless steel prong buckle completes the reference. Caliber 26-330 S C J, self-winding, powers the movement.

Where Genta's contemporaneous designs emphasised geometric angularity, the Polo pursued organic continuity — the case disappearing into the bracelet so completely that the watch reads as a single sculptural object rather than a case with a strap attached. The ladies' 23mm configuration in all-yellow gold is the Polo at its most jewelry-concentrated, the small oval case barely perceptible within the continuous gold ribbon of the bracelet.

 The 23mm yellow gold oval case carries the characteristic horizontal fluting running across the case middle, integrating seamlessly with the wider ribbed bracelet links above and below. The gold dial presents dot hour markers at each hour position and gold baton hands, the minimalist layout preserving the dial's visual continuity with the surrounding gold surfaces. The integrated yellow gold bracelet tapers from the case with uniformly fluted rectangular links. A Swiss quartz movement powers the watch.

The Cartier Santos Medium W2SA0016 holds a unique position in watchmaking history as the world's first purpose-built aviator's wristwatch — created in 1904 by Louis Cartier for Brazilian aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont, who required a timepiece readable during flight without removing his hands from the controls. The watch introduced the exposed screw on the bezel as a functional and subsequently iconic design element, a detail that has defined the Santos's visual identity across twelve decades of continuous evolution. The current Santos de Cartier, reintroduced in 2018 with a refined case architecture and the QuickSwitch interchangeable strap system, represents the most technically developed generation of the reference, and the medium two-tone stainless steel and yellow gold configuration is among the most historically faithful — closest in spirit to the original, which also combined two materials in its construction.

 The medium stainless steel case carries a yellow gold bezel secured by eight polished yellow gold screws — the Santos's defining decorative and structural motif. The white silvered dial presents bold black Roman numerals, a fine inner railroad minute track, and blued-steel sword hands with a sapphire cabochon crown. The integrated bracelet alternates stainless steel and yellow gold links in matching two-tone construction, with a double-blade deployant clasp. Caliber 1847 MC, automatic, powers the movement.

 *This timepiece comes with an additional leather strap, original white hang tag, buckle, and screwdriver.

items.model: Patek Philippe Grand Complications 5208/300P-010 Minute Repeater Perpetual Calendar Chronograph Platinum Salmon Dial Diamond Baguette Bezel (2021)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Patek Philippe Grand Complications 5208/300P-010 is among the most mechanically ambitious wristwatches in continuous production anywhere in the world — a single case containing an instantaneous perpetual calendar, a minute repeater, and a monopusher chronograph, three complications that individually represent the highest tier of mechanical watchmaking and which, combined in a self-winding movement, require a construction of extraordinary sophistication. Caliber R CH 27 PS QI achieves this integration automatically through a 22K gold micro-rotor — a decision that distinguishes the 5208 from most other minute repeater wristwatches, which are traditionally manually wound. The 5208/300P-010 presents the reference in platinum with a continuous baguette-cut diamond bezel and a salmon sunburst dial — a color associated across the collector community with some of the most coveted Patek Philippe variants — elevating an already rarefied horological achievement into haute joaillerie.

 The platinum case carries a bezel set with a continuous row of baguette-cut diamonds. The salmon sunburst dial presents applied baton hour markers, subsidiary dials for small seconds at nine and chronograph counter at three, a moon phase at six, and instantaneous perpetual calendar apertures for day, date, and month. White gold hands complete the dial. A black alligator strap with platinum fold-over clasp completes the reference. Caliber R CH 27 PS QI, automatic with micro-rotor, 719 parts, powers the watch.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The 5236's in-line perpetual calendar is the most legibility-focused perpetual calendar display Patek Philippe has ever produced — day, date, and month aligned horizontally in a single large aperture at twelve o'clock, readable in a single glance without any requirement to cross-reference subsidiary dials. The mechanism enabling this layout is covered by three separate patents, addressing the engineering challenges of driving three independently advancing indicators from a single aperture position within the footprint of an ultra-thin self-winding movement. At 503 parts and 55 jewels, caliber 31-260 PS QL is among the most component-dense self-winding perpetual calendar movements in the manufacture's current catalogue. The 5236P-011 introduces this complication in platinum for the first time alongside a silvery vertical satin-finish dial with graduating black rim — a restrained palette that places maximum visual emphasis on the aperture display at twelve.

 The 41.3mm fully polished platinum case carries a diamond at six o'clock and a sapphire crystal case back. The silvery dial with vertical satin-finish and black-gradient rim presents charcoal gray white gold applied faceted baton hour markers and matching hands. The triple in-line aperture at twelve displays day, date, and month simultaneously; leap year and day/night indicators appear in round apertures; small seconds and moon phases sit at six. A charcoal gray composite fabric-pattern strap with cream stitching and platinum triple-blade fold-over clasp completes the reference.

items.sourceDescription:
The split-seconds chronograph with perpetual calendar occupies a category entirely its own within haute horlogerie — a combination so mechanically demanding that only a handful of manufacturers worldwide produce it in-house, and among those, fewer still do so in a manually wound caliber. Patek Philippe's CHR 29-535 PS Q, with its two column wheels, horizontal clutch, and 496 parts, has been the benchmark for this complication since its introduction; the 5204G-010 brings it to white gold for the first time alongside a navy blue sunburst dial whose red split-seconds and 30-minute counter hands make the split function's purpose immediately legible to any observer — a design decision that acknowledges the complication's athletic origins in precision timing without compromising the watch's formal authority. The dual strap set supplied with each example — fabric and alligator, both with red stitching — extends that versatility further.

 The 40mm fully polished white gold case carries interchangeable solid and sapphire crystal case backs. The sunburst navy blue dial presents white gold applied faceted "obus" hour markers, white gold faceted dauphine hands with luminescence, and a printed white tachymeter scale. Red split-seconds and 30-minute counter hands provide chromatic contrast; a day/month double aperture at twelve, moon phases and date hand at six, and small seconds at nine complete the perpetual calendar and chronograph display. Both navy blue fabric and dark blue alligator straps with red stitching and white gold triple-blade fold-over clasp are included.

The 7047G-001 is the most unusual minute repeater in Patek Philippe's 2026 Grand Complications programme — a reference that deploys the manufacture's most acoustically demanding complication within a new 38mm Calatrava case of demonstrably sporting character, with a colour language drawn from athletic rather than formal references. The minute repeater is classically considered the most technically challenging of all watch complications to execute correctly, requiring the careful voicing and tuning of two steel gongs to produce tones of musical clarity; the R 27 PS caliber's chime on two classic gongs represents one of the highest acoustic achievements in contemporary self-winding repeater watchmaking. The decision to place this movement in a navy-and-orange context — carbon-embossed dial centre, orange small seconds hand, orange triangle hour markers — positions the 7047G-001 as a deliberate argument that the minute repeater need not be confined to formal evening contexts.

 The 38mm polished white gold case carries a sapphire crystal case back. The navy blue dial on an 18K gold plate presents three distinct surface treatments: a snailed inner minute scale, a circular satin-finished hour circle, and a sunburst outer minute scale. White gold applied luminous numerals and baton hands are set against orange transfer-printed triangle markers, with an orange varnished small seconds hand at six o'clock. A navy blue composite fabric-pattern strap with orange stitching and lining, secured by a white gold prong buckle, completes the reference.

items.model: Patek Philippe Complications 5249R-001 Hours And Minutes On Demand Automaton 'The Crow and the Fox' Rose Gold Matara (2026)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The 5249R-001 ' The Crow and the Fox' is Patek Philippe's first automaton wristwatch in the manufacture's contemporary history — a reference that traces its lineage directly to a pocket watch Louis Cottier designed for Patek Philippe in 1958, now preserved in the Patek Philippe Museum, which depicted La Fontaine's fable of the Crow and the Fox using the same on-demand retrograde time display mechanism. The complication operates by pressing the pusher at two o'clock: two curved retrograde scales spring forward to display hours and minutes while the applied gold fox and crow figures animate on the dial surface, then the scales retract and the animals return to their positions among the hand-engraved foliage. The translation of a 1958 pocket watch concept into a self-winding wristwatch caliber — achieved through the purpose-built 31-260 PS HMD AU — represents one of the most technically demanding horological projects in the 2026 calendar year.

 The 43mm rose gold Officer's-style case carries a sapphire crystal case back protected by a dust cover with invisible hinges. The opaline matara brown dial on an 18K gold plate presents applied fox and crow figures in contrasting colours amid hand-engraved gold foliage, with two curved retrograde scales for hours and minutes activated on demand. A shiny chocolate brown square-scale alligator strap with rose gold triple-blade fold-over clasp completes the reference. Caliber 31-260 PS HMD AU, self-winding with platinum off-center minirotor, powers the movement.

This piece was recently unveiled at Watches & Wonders 2026 — please register your interest for priority access as soon as we are able to secure it for you.

The patinated green alligator strap — its colour applied through a traditional hand-patination process — extends the chromatic commitment from case to wrist, making the 5322G-010 a fully resolved design object from every angle.

 The 41mm white gold case carries hobnail guilloché on the entire caseband and pusher, with skeletonized lugs and sapphire crystal case back. The alarm mechanism's four patents address the core challenge of integrating a striking function with water resistance while maintaining the acoustic properties expected of a Grand Complication. The 24-hour alarm display — shown digitally in aperture in 15-minute increments, with separate day/night and on/off apertures — represents a more intuitive and legible alarm interface than any traditional alarm watch Patek Philippe has previously produced. Caliber AL 30-660 S C achieves 524 parts within 6.6mm of movement thickness, a miniaturization achievement that makes the hobnail-guilloché Calatrava case at 12.22mm remarkably contained for its content.

 The 41mm white gold Calatrava case carries hobnail guilloché on the entire caseband and pusher, with skeletonized lugs and sapphire crystal case back. A navy blue composite fabric strap with cream stitching and white gold triple-blade fold-over clasp — plus a beige nubuck calfskin strap — complete the reference.
