items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The 6105G-001 Celestial Sunrise and Sunset is among the most conceptually ambitious watches Patek Philippe has produced — a 47mm Grand Complication that required more than five years of development, six patents, and 426 movement components to display not just the time but the actual configuration of the night sky as visible from Geneva. Caliber 240 C LU CL LCSO maps stellar positions, the Moon's phases and orbit, the meridian passage of Sirius, and now adds sunrise and sunset time indications plus a patented corrector system that automatically adjusts all celestial displays during daylight saving transitions — a complication that solves a genuinely practical problem no prior astronomical watch has addressed. The 6105G-001's space module-inspired case architecture signals its scientific ambition visually: sandblasted flanks, patterned case back, and correctors at two and four o'clock distinguish it immediately from any preceding Celestial.

 The 47mm white gold case carries contrasting polished and sandblasted finishes with space module patterning on the flanks and solid case back, and correctors at two and four o'clock for seasonal time adjustment. The sapphire crystal dial depicts the northern hemisphere sky as seen from Geneva — stars, the Milky Way, an elliptical visibility horizon, the Moon with its phases and orbit — with dedicated hands for sunrise, sunset, date, and meridian passage, plus skeletonized white gold baton hands for mean solar time. A black composite X-patterned strap with white gold fold-over clasp completes the reference.

 This piece was recently unveiled at Watches & Wonders 2026 — please register your interest for priority access as soon as we are able to secure it for you.

At 38mm in platinum with the integrated three-link bracelet, the 5610/1P-001 occupies a size register that historically has been assigned to Ladies' and transitional Nautilus references, and the result is a watch that carries the full visual authority of the Nautilus design language with a discretion the larger editions cannot achieve. The platinum case introduces a distinctly cooler and denser wrist presence than white gold — the metal's greater specific gravity is perceptible on the wrist, and its characteristic grey tone reads differently against the sunburst blue dial than either white gold would. A single diamond set at nine o'clock marks the reference's status quietly.

 The 38mm two-part platinum case carries contrasting polished and satin finishes, a diamond set at nine o'clock, a screw-down crown, and a sapphire crystal case back. The sunburst blue horizontally embossed dial presents white gold applied baton-style hour markers and white gold rounded baton hands, both with luminescent coating. The integrated platinum bracelet with patented fold-over clasp and lockable adjustment system completes the reference. Caliber 240, ultra-thin self-winding with anniversary-engraved 22K gold minirotor, powers the movement.

Limited Edition of 2000.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Among the most extraordinary diplomatic and royal commission watches produced by any Swiss manufacture, this Jaeger-LeCoultre Secret Hours was made specifically for presentation within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia — an object that functions simultaneously as a precision timepiece, a jewellery object, and a state gift. The case lid is set with an authentic Saudi Arabian gold coin bearing the royal seal and Arabic calligraphic inscriptions, its relief engraving transformed into the watch's exterior face; lifting the hinged coin reveals the malachite dial beneath. The Secret Hours complication — in which the dial is concealed behind a decorated cover that opens to reveal the time — has appeared in some of the most celebrated Jaeger-LeCoultre commissions in the manufacture's history, and the Saudi coin version represents the most diplomatically charged application of this concept, combining numismatic provenance with Swiss horological craft in a single object of genuinely singular significance.

 The 30mm yellow gold round case carries the hinged Saudi gold coin as its cover, its edge engraved with fine rope detailing echoing the integrated herringbone-weave yellow gold bracelet. Opening the coin reveals a deep malachite dial displaying the natural mineral's characteristic parallel banding in rich green tones, set with gold baton hour markers and gold hands. The integrated yellow gold herringbone-weave bracelet with fold-over clasp completes the piece. A Swiss manual movement powers the watch.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Golden Ellipse is Patek Philippe's most mathematically resolved design — a case form derived from the golden ratio of 1:1.618, introduced in 1968 and unchanged in its essential proportions ever since. At 5.9mm thick, the 3738/100G stands as the thinnest watch in the entire Golden Ellipse range, its remarkably slim profile made possible by caliber 240's 2.53mm movement thickness — the same ultra-thin movement that powers the Calatrava 7200/50G. The Rolex Yacht-Master 16622 holds a distinguished position in the Yacht-Master lineage as the original 40mm configuration, produced from 1999 through 2012 before being succeeded by the 116622. Its defining material proposition — a stainless steel case paired with a solid platinum bidirectional rotating bezel — remains unique within the broader Rolex catalog, representing the only reference of its era to combine these two metals in this manner. Among collectors tracking the pre-ceramic Yacht-Master generation, the 16622 is now a closed reference with a finite production window, and examples in unworn or lightly worn condition command consistent premiums reflecting that scarcity.

 The 40mm stainless steel Oyster case carries a solid platinum bezel with raised, polished pip and minute graduation markings, its bidirectional rotation distinguishing it functionally from the Submariner's unidirectional dive bezel. The silver dial presents luminous round hour markers, rectangular indexes at three, six, and nine, and a characteristic red seconds hand, with a date aperture at three o'clock beneath a Cyclops lens. The three-link Oyster bracelet in stainless steel with an Oysterlock clasp completes the reference. Caliber 3135 powers the movement.

The platinum case construction with black dial creates elegant visual contrast making this among the most sophisticated yet understated references in Patek Philippe's current collection, appealing to collectors who value both technical complexity combining chronograph and annual calendar complications in elegant classical round case architecture and platinum's prestigious status as the manufacture's most exclusive case material.

 The 40.5mm case crafted in platinum features polished round bezel, brushed case band, straight lugs with polished surfaces, sapphire crystal, two chronograph pushers at 2 and 4 o'clock positions for start/stop and reset functions, recessed correctors in case band for independent adjustment of day, date, and month, and transparent sapphire caseback revealing the extensively decorated movement. Inside beats the self-winding Caliber CH 28-520 QA 24H featuring column-wheel chronograph mechanism with vertical clutch ensuring smooth chronograph hand start, annual calendar complication with instantaneous jump for all calendar indications at midnight, 24-hour display, central rotor in 21-karat gold, 40 jewels, Gyromax balance wheel, Spiromax balance spring in Silinvar silicon, frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour, Patek Philippe Seal certification guaranteeing exceptional finishing and precision standards of minus three to plus two seconds per day, approximately 45 to 55 hours of power reserve. Represents Richard Mille's avant-garde reinterpretation of erotic timepiece tradition dating back centuries to 18th-19th century pocket watches featuring suggestive mechanized scenes often banned and confiscated by conservative moral, religious, political authorities yet enjoyed secretly away from prying eyes. Launched 2015 developed collaboration with Audemars Piguet Renaud & Papi, RM 69 modernizes historical theme through less graphic, subtler approach displaying random suggestive messages via three engraved grade 5 titanium rollers functioning like Tibetan prayer wheels or slot machine reels generating combinations including phrases "I long to," "let me," "I need to," paired with "arouse," "explore," complemented by "your lips," "your nipples," "you tonight." Limited strictly to 30 pieces worldwide sold exclusively through Richard Mille boutiques representing brand's ability selling such unconventional watches through centimillionaire clientele. Unusual movement construction featuring barrel positioned directly beneath tourbillon sharing same central axis creates compact architecture allowing space for Oracle complication while maintaining 69-hour power reserve through single barrel.

 The 50mm x 42.70mm x 16.15mm tripartite tonneau-shaped case crafted entirely in grade 5 titanium (90% titanium, 6% aluminum, 4% vanadium alloy used in aerospace, aeronautics, automobile industries) features ergonomic curved design, assembled with 20 spline screws in titanium, sapphire crystal front and back, 50m water resistance. Openworked skeletonized dial reveals three engraved grade 5 titanium rollers displaying random message combinations, tourbillon at 6 o'clock, power reserve indicator aperture at 4 o'clock powered by planetary differential, retractable hour and minute hands. Pusher at 10 o'clock activates roller rotation like slot machine spinning briefly before stopping on random combination. Pusher at 8 o'clock retracts hands clearing visual obstruction allowing unobstructed message legibility—hands automatically return to proper position when released. Manual-winding Caliber RM069 features 505 components, 41 jewels, 32.80mm x 30.90mm x 10.26mm dimensions, tourbillon regulator with Glucydur balance, free-sprung balance for shock protection, 3 Hz frequency (21,600 vph), fast-rotating barrel, 69-hour power reserve, grade 5 titanium baseplate and bridges, circular-graining, beveling, mirror-finishing, hand-polished sinks paired with PVD-treated micro-blasted satin-finished surfaces. Black rubber strap with titanium double-fold deployant clasp.

 *This is a limited edition of 30 pieces.

items.model: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak 25654ST.OO.0944ST.01 Perpetual Calendar Stainless Steel Silver Dial Limited Edition of 272
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 25654ST.OO.0944ST.01 houses a delicate perpetual calendar complication within a steel case, and proved mind-boggling in 1984 when few manufacturers still produced perpetual calendars, Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar representing first luxury sports watch featuring complication. The 39mm diameter matches original 1972 Royal Oak "Jumbo" reference 5402's sizing, Audemars Piguet carefully retaining iconic proportions while integrating full perpetual calendar display maintaining watch's signature svelte profile contrasting muscular presence with aquiline thinness. First-generation reference 5554 featured smooth dials without tapisserie guilloché, reference 25654 continued primarily with smooth dials though some tapisserie examples exist. Two dial generations identifiable (Series C and D) recognizable through Audemars Piguet typography evolution in early 1990s, silver dial variant representing classic configuration. This non-leap-year indicator model (production ceased 1993 though sales continued until 1998) eventually succeeded by reference 25820 introducing leap-year cycle display through modified Caliber 2120/2802.

 The 39mm case measures 8.25mm thick (9.3mm including crystal), crafted entirely in brushed stainless steel with case sculpted from massive steel chunk featuring angular beveled edges and alternating brushed/polished surfaces requiring meticulous hand-finishing. The octagonal bezel secured by eight exposed hexagonal screws (crafted in contrasting white gold on this example) represents Royal Oak's most iconic design element, screws serving structural role passing completely through two-part case holding assembly together impermeable to water intrusion. The bezel's polished finish contrasts dramatically against brushed case and bracelet surfaces while case side bevels add architectural complexity to profile. Sapphire crystal protects dial while solid caseback maintains structural integrity and improved water resistance versus predecessor. The silver dial without tapisserie guilloché represents early-generation aesthetic preferred by collectors, smooth surface allowing unobstructed appreciation of perpetual calendar complications' layout. Four subdials present traditional perpetual calendar indications: day at 9 o'clock, astronomical moonphase with graduation for moon age at 6 o'clock, month at 12 o'clock, and date at 3 o'clock, each subsidiary dial featuring blued hands matching blued moonphase wheel adding subtle color accent against silver background. Applied baton hour markers and matching baton hands maintain Royal Oak's characteristic clean aesthetic while ensuring legibility, lack of leap-year indicator distinguishing this early non-leap-year variant from later 1995-2014 production introducing leap-year display. Dial signature typography identifies Series C or D generation depending on production period. Perpetual calendar adjustment accomplished through pushers located along case sides: two on left side, one on right side, allowing independent setting of day, date, and month complications. The self-winding Caliber 2120/2800 represents legendary ultra-thin movement initially developed by Jaeger-LeCoultre as Caliber 920 in 1967 (funded and contributed by Audemars Piguet), measuring just 3.95mm thickness making it world's thinnest perpetual calendar movement until 2019's introduction of modern ultra-thin calibers. The movement comprises 292 individual components with 38 jewels, Gyromax balance adjusted to heat, cold, isochronism and five positions ensuring chronometric precision. Full-diameter rotor runs on beryllium rail for stability, four ruby wheels supporting rotor's operation, 21k gold segment increasing rotor mass improving automatic winding efficiency. The base 2120 remains world's thinnest full-rotor self-winding movement considered by many as one of most technically refined wristwatch movements ever produced, its adoption by Audemars Piguet, Patek Philippe (Nautilus), and Vacheron Constantin (222) demonstrating universal respect for design. Perpetual calendar module 2800 added atop base 2120 creating complete Caliber 2120/2800 designation. Integrated stainless steel bracelet features Royal Oak's signature two rows of inner links expertly finished with alternating brushed surfaces and high-polished beveled edges, bracelet's mechanical integration flowing seamlessly from lugs representing Gerald Genta's original 1972 vision. AP logo-shaped single folding clasp with trigger release provides secure closure while maintaining clean aesthetic.

 *This timepiece is a limited edition of 272 pieces, and comes with Archive Papers.

items.model: Patek Philippe Celestial Joaillerie Grand Complications 6104/13P-010 Platinum Blue Dial Emerald Bezel
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Grand Complications 6104/13P-010 represents ultra-rare out-of-catalogue variant reserved exclusively for Patek Philippe's most important collectors. The 60 baguette-cut emeralds totaling 3.92 carats distributed across bezel (38 stones, 3.04 carats) and platinum fold-over clasp (22 stones, 0.88 carat) provide vibrant green frame complementing blue celestial dial depicting nocturnal sky visible from Geneva latitude. Emerald variant's lower total carat weight versus sapphire (6.04 total carats) or ruby (5.66 total carats) reflects emeralds' lower density—stones cut to same approximate physical dimensions weigh less, though procurement difficulty and value premium far exceed corundum (sapphire/ruby) alternatives. The Celestial complication traces lineage to Patek Philippe's 1985 Reference 3874 Caliber 240 featuring astronomical indications, with modern 6104 series debuted 2002 offering rotating sky chart, moon phase orbit, and sidereal time within 44mm case powered by ultra-thin Caliber 240 LU CL C. The astronomical display presents exact configuration of nocturnal sky in northern hemisphere at any moment, apparent movement of stars and moon phases/orbit visible through rotating sapphire disk.

 The 44mm case measures 11.33mm thick despite housing complex astronomical complications, crafted entirely in 950 platinum with polished surfaces throughout maintaining classical elegance appropriate for grand complication dress watch positioning. The bezel set with 38 baguette-cut emeralds creates vibrant green border framing dial, each stone precision-cut to fit curved bezel geometry while maintaining uniform appearance and secure channel setting protecting stones during wear. Water resistance limited to 30 meters reflects dress watch orientation prioritizing case refinement over sports watch robustness, sapphire crystals front and back allowing unobstructed viewing of astronomical display and exhibition caseback revealing Caliber 240 LU CL C's architecture. Brilliant-cut diamond set at 6 o'clock position provides subtle accent complementing emerald bezel while maintaining symmetry. The rotating blue sapphire crystal disk depicts celestial map showing Milky Way, stars, and constellation patterns visible from Geneva and all cities at same latitude (approximately 46 degrees north), ellipse deposited on sapphire crystal's underside frames visible sky portion while disk rotates counterclockwise completing full revolution every 23 hours 56 minutes matching actual sidereal day (star time versus solar time). White gold skeletonized leaf-shaped hands indicate hours and minutes of mean solar time atop rotating celestial display, hands' openworked construction minimizing visual obstruction of star chart beneath. Moon phase indication shows lunar orbit and current phase through aperture with high precision requiring correction only once every 122 years, meridian passage of Sirius (brightest star in night sky) marked for astronomical reference. The self-winding Caliber 240 LU CL C measures 38mm diameter by 6.81mm thickness representing ultra-thin movement construction enabling relatively modest case profile despite complication complexity, movement comprises 315 components with 45 jewels operating at 21,600 semi-oscillations per hour (3Hz) with 38-48 hour power reserve. The 22k gold off-center mini-rotor enables automatic winding while maintaining movement thinness versus traditional central rotor, Gyromax balance ensures precision timekeeping through adjustable inertia blocks eliminating regulator index. The "LU" designation indicates lunar (moon) complications while "CL" signifies celestial (star chart) functions, movement finishing includes Geneva Seal standards with hand-beveled edges, circular graining, and polished steel parts visible through sapphire caseback. Hand-stitched shiny navy blue alligator leather strap with square scales complements celestial dial while platinum fold-over clasp set with 22 baguette-cut emeralds (0.88 carat) extends gem-set luxury beyond case, clasp's emerald integration creating cohesive jewelry presentation across entire timepiece visible even when worn.

items.model: Rolex Day-Date 36 128236 Platinum Ice Blue Roman Numerals Dial (2023)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Introduced Watches & Wonders 2022, reference 128236 represents watershed moment in  Day-Date platinum history—debuting platinum fluted bezel for first time after decades exclusively pairing platinum cases with smooth domed bezels on references 118206/128206. Rolex explained that until 2022, manufacturing platinum fluted bezel proved technically impossible due to platinum's challenging machining and polishing characteristics compared to gold—the metal's density and work-hardening properties requiring entirely new manufacturing processes before fluted bezel could enter platinum production. From 2022 forward, platinum Day-Date available exclusively with either platinum fluted bezel or diamond-set bezel, eliminating smooth domed bezel option that previously distinguished platinum from gold variants. The ice blue dial color remains exclusive signature of platinum Rolex models—appearing only on platinum Day-Date and certain platinum Daytona variants—serving as immediate visual identifier of watch's precious metal construction without requiring close inspection. This sunray-finished ice blue shade creates cool, sophisticated aesthetic contrasting against platinum's naturally white metallic luster while Roman numerals on 36mm version feature smoother overall shape and finish versus sharper, more angular Roman numerals found on 40mm Day-Date variant. The 36mm proportions represent classic Day-Date sizing dating to 1956 original introduction, balanced diameter offering elegant wrist presence appropriate for formal dress watch positioning while 950 platinum construction provides substantial heft and density exceeding gold variants.

 The 36mm Oyster case measures approximately 12mm thick, crafted entirely in 950 platinum with monobloc middle case ensuring structural integrity and water resistance. The platinum fluted bezel features Rolex's signature triangular ridges creating interplay between polished and brushed surfaces catching light dynamically, the fluting's introduction to platinum requiring years' development given metal's challenging machining properties versus traditional gold applications. Screw-down caseback and Twinlock double waterproofness system crown ensure 100-meter water resistance appropriate for presidential dress watch despite formal positioning, the Oyster architecture maintaining sports watch DNA within elegant context. Scratch-resistant sapphire crystal with Cyclops lens magnifying date aperture at 3 o'clock maintains legibility while glareproofing treatment reduces reflections. The ice blue sunray dial exhibits subtle radial brushing emanating from center creating dynamic surface catching light differently based on viewing angle, the cool blue tone exclusive to platinum Rolex models serving as understated precious metal indicator. Applied Roman numeral hour markers crafted from platinum feature smoother contours on 36mm variant versus 40mm's sharper, more angular execution, filled with white luminescent material ensuring low-light legibility despite formal aesthetic. Day aperture at 12 o'clock displays full weekday name in choice of 26 languages while date at 3 o'clock benefits from Cyclops magnification, both complications featuring instantaneous midnight changeover with secure rapid-setting mechanism allowing independent adjustment without affecting timekeeping precision. The self-winding Caliber 3255 introduced 2015 represents Rolex's latest generation perpetual movement comprising 14 patents with 70-hour power reserve enabling weekend autonomy when removed Friday evening. The movement achieves Superlative Chronometer certification guaranteeing -2/+2 seconds daily accuracy after casing (exceeding COSC's ±4 seconds standard), incorporating paramagnetic blue Parachrom hairspring offering superior shock and temperature resistance plus Paraflex shock absorbers protecting balance assembly. Bidirectional self-winding via Perpetual rotor ensures efficient energy transfer while Chronergy escapement patented by Rolex increases reliability and power reserve versus traditional Swiss lever escapements. The semi-circular three-piece link President bracelet crafted entirely in 950 platinum flows seamlessly from lugs, the bracelet's supple articulation and substantial weight creating luxurious wearing experience. Concealed folding Crownclasp maintains clean aesthetic eliminating visible clasp mechanisms while Easylink 5mm comfort extension allows fine-tuning fit throughout day as wrist expands.

items.model: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak 67630OR.OO.1312OR.01-B 'Mini' Rose Gold Black Onyx Diamond Dial Quartz (2026)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Introduced early 2026, reference 67630OR.OO.1312OR.01-B extends  Royal Oak Mini lineup introduced 2024 with new stone dial variants deepening connection between watchmaking and jewelry. Following 2024's Frosted Gold editions featuring Carolina Bucci's diamond-tipped micro-hammering technique creating luminous frost effect across tone-on-tone Petite Tapisserie dials, 2026's releases shift focus toward natural stone dials—white mother of pearl and polished black onyx—paired with traditional polished rose gold or yellow gold construction without hammered finish. The polished black onyx dial exhibits uniform high-gloss surface creating bold statement through deep black tone contrasting dramatically against warm 18k rose gold architecture, the stone's natural density and opacity providing perfect backdrop for brilliant-cut diamond hour markers creating hypnotic play of light against dark surface. Where Frosted Gold variants emphasized metal surface treatment and white mother of pearl celebrated organic iridescence, black onyx variant pursues maximum contrast and jewelry presence through dramatic color juxtaposition and gemstone integration. The Royal Oak Mini concept originated with 1997's "Mini Oak" targeted at smaller wrists, revived 2024 after years' absence with 23mm proportions positioning watch as jewelry-forward accessory emphasizing decorative appeal over primary timekeeping function—dainty and delicate interpretation transforming Royal Oak's traditionally bold, sporty character into feminine, refined presentation where precious materials and gemstones take precedence over horological complexity.

 The 23mm case measures 6.6mm thick, crafted entirely in polished 18k rose gold with octagonal bezel secured by eight exposed hexagonal screws with perfectly aligned slots maintaining Royal Oak's signature industrial-luxury design language despite miniaturized proportions. The alternating satin brushing and polished bevels across case surfaces demonstrate meticulous hand-finishing translating Royal Oak's architectural geometry to jewelry scale where each surface transition requires individual craftsman attention during manufacture. Glareproofed sapphire crystal protects dial while maintaining crystal-clear visibility showcasing polished onyx's rich tones and diamond markers' brilliant sparkle, though exhibition caseback omitted in favor of solid construction given quartz movement's limited visual appeal versus mechanical counterparts. Water resistance reaches 50 meters appropriate for casual water exposure including handwashing and rain though not intended for swimming or immersion, the 50-meter rating notable performance for jewelry watch of this compact size. Introduced early 2026, reference 26450ST represents most significant upgrade in 38mm  Royal Oak Chronograph history—introducing entirely new in-house Caliber 6401 after nearly three decades utilizing Frédéric Piguet 1185 ébauche (rebranded Caliber 2385). The development spanning five years delivers not downsized version of 41mm's Caliber 4401 but complete reimagining optimized specifically for smaller proportions. Patented vertical clutch simplified to reduce mechanical complexity while improving pusher feel, directly driven design positioned centrally removes intermediate transmission wheels enhancing start/stop precision. The dial layout redesigned for enhanced legibility: subdials repositioned further from center with 30-minute totalizer moved to 9 o'clock (previously 3), 12-hour counter relocated to 3 o'clock (previously 9), running seconds at 6 o'clock now featuring Arabic numerals at 20/40/60 for improved timing readability. Date window shifted midway between 4-5 o'clock maintaining better symmetry. Power reserve increased to 72 hours from predecessor's 40 hours representing 80% improvement addressing long-standing limitation while beat rate elevated to 28,800 vph (4Hz) from predecessor's 21,600 vph improving precision and chronograph accuracy. Most notably, sapphire exhibition caseback debuts for first time in 38mm Royal Oak Chronograph's history revealing movement finishing previously hidden beneath solid steel caseback—major transparency upgrade demonstrating confidence in Caliber 6401's decoration quality.

 The 38mm case measures 11.1mm thick representing minimal 0.1mm increase over predecessor despite housing entirely new movement architecture, crafted in brushed stainless steel with octagonal bezel secured by eight exposed hexagonal screws with perfectly aligned slots. The blue Grande Tapisserie dial features Royal Oak's original large-scale waffle pattern creating architectural depth through light and shadow interplay, the pattern's geometric precision requiring specialized stamping dies and multiple manufacturing steps to achieve consistent relief depth. Three blue tone-on-tone chronograph subdials with snailed finishing provide subtle textural variation: 30-minute totalizer at 9 o'clock, 12-hour counter at 3 o'clock, running seconds at 6 o'clock with white Arabic numerals at 20/40/60 improving legibility during chronograph timing. Applied 18k white gold baton hour markers and matching Royal Oak hands filled with white luminescent material ensure visibility in low-light conditions while rhodium-toned inner bezel frames composition. The self-winding Caliber 6401 comprises 348 components with 44 jewels, operating at 28,800 vph with robust 72-hour power reserve representing significant improvement over predecessor's 40-50 hours. The movement showcases exceptional hand-finishing visible through sapphire caseback including straight-grained mainplate, beveled edges, and circular-grained ratchet wheel.  The 41mm case measures 10.6mm thick, combining 18k white gold for the round bezel and caseback with black ceramic octagonal middle section—signature Code 11.59 construction framing the round outer elements around geometric core. items.model: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 26674CD.OO.1225CD.01 Bleu Nuit Nuage 50 Blue Ceramic (2026)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Released early 2026, the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 26674CD.OO.1225CD.01 "Bleu Nuit, Nuage 50" ceramic unites two pivotal Audemars Piguet developments: the historically rooted deep blue ceramic introduced during 2025's 150th anniversary celebrations and the revolutionary Caliber 7138 perpetual calendar movement. The ceramic shade references the night sky above Vallée de Joux—same inspiration behind Gerald Genta's dark blue dial for the original 1972 Royal Oak reference 5402. When Genta commissioned Geneva dial maker Stern to replicate that nocturnal color, they created signature "Bleu Nuit, Nuage 50" by adding pigment number 50 to protective Zapon varnish, with "cloud" effect resulting from pouring black into liquid lacquer. While original dials used chemical reactions to achieve this, modern production employs PVD process for homogeneous tone. Translating this color to ceramic presented entirely different challenge—requiring several years' development to ensure consistent results across case, bezel, and bracelet components. The achievement represents significant departure from AP's previous bright cobalt blue ceramics. Tom Brady wore this watch during Super Bowl pre-game festivities alongside Green Day, bringing immediate collector attention to the release.

 The 41mm case measures a remarkably slim 9.5mm despite housing the full perpetual calendar complication, crafted entirely in "Bleu Nuit, Nuage 50" ceramic with satin-brushed surfaces and polished bevels that maintain the Royal Oak's signature sharp geometry—a significant technical achievement given ceramic's amorphous structure compared to traditional metals. The octagonal bezel secured by eight white gold screws with perfectly aligned slots sits atop the integrated case construction, while a titanium caseback with sapphire exhibition window reveals the movement within, framed by precisely beveled ceramic work. Water resistance reaches 50 meters, substantially improved from the previous generation's 20 meters thanks to Caliber 7138's elimination of multiple case apertures for correctors. The blue Grande Tapisserie dial creates a monochromatic field perfectly matching the ceramic case, with matching blue subdials and inner bezel contrasted by applied 18k white gold hour markers and Royal Oak hands filled with luminescent material. The perpetual calendar displays are logically arranged without crowding: day indication at 9 o'clock incorporates a 24-hour indicator with red non-correction zone warning, a large instantaneous jumping date aperture commands 12 o'clock, month and leap year share the 3 o'clock position, while an astronomical moonphase at 6 o'clock features realistic NASA-based lunar surface imagery rather than traditional romantic depictions. Peripheral week indication runs along the dial edge against a white printed minute track. Powering this monochromatic achievement is the self-winding Caliber 7138 measuring 29.6mm diameter by 4.1mm thickness, comprising 423 components with 41 jewels operating at 28,800 vph with 55-hour power reserve. The movement's revolutionary patented all-in-one crown adjustment system features four positions enabling all calendar functions to be set solely via the screw-locked ceramic crown without recessed correctors, tools, or risk of mechanism damage—even during traditional danger zones marked in red. A 48-tooth wheel pre-programmed with month lengths across the quadrennial leap year cycle means the watch requires no correction until year 2100. The integrated "Bleu Nuit, Nuage 50" ceramic bracelet flows seamlessly from case to clasp, its lightweight nature belying the watch's substantial presence while the exceptional scratch resistance of ceramic ensures the deep blue finish endures. An AP three-blade titanium folding clasp secures the bracelet.

 This piece was recently unveiled. To express interest, please inquire above and our team will contact you once we are able to secure it for you.

items.model: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 26685XT.OO.1320XT.01 Titanium BMG Openworked Dial (2026)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar 26685XT.OO.1320XT.01, released in early 2026, represents evolutionary leap for Audemars Piguet's perpetual calendar platform—introducing revolutionary Caliber 7139 openworked movement that transforms user interaction with haute horology's most intellectually complex complication. Where previous Royal Oak perpetual calendars required recessed correctors accessed via stylus or toothpick for calendar adjustments—anxiety-inducing proposition—Caliber 7139 accomplishes all functions through crown alone via patented all-in-one adjustment system with four positions. This crown-only operation eliminates multiple case apertures, enabling water resistance increase from previous generation's 20 meters to meaningful 50 meters—making this first Royal Oak perpetual calendar safe for swimming. The movement builds upon 2025's groundbreaking Caliber 7138 (introduced alongside ceramic Bleu Nuit variant) while adding openworked architecture revealing mechanical artistry. Royal Oak perpetual calendars trace lineage to 1984's reference 5554—world's first luxury sports watch perpetual calendar combining Gerald Genta's iconic integrated-bracelet design with sophisticated complications. This titanium/BMG variant replaces 2025's 150th Anniversary limited edition, signaling generational shift toward improved ergonomics without sacrificing visual spectacle.

 The 41mm case measures remarkably slim at 9.5mm thick—0.4mm thinner than predecessor—combining lightweight Grade 5 titanium with Audemars Piguet's proprietary Bulk Metallic Glass (BMG), amorphous palladium-based metallic alloy (approximately 50% palladium weight) whose atoms arrange like glass rather than ordered crystalline structure. BMG features distinctive mirror-like polish with exceptional scratch resistance measuring approximately 500 Vickers hardness—dramatically harder than platinum's 90-140 HV that plagued earlier polished Royal Oak bezels. BMG is utilized for the octagonal bezel secured by eight polished hexagonal screws with perfectly aligned slots, caseback frame, and bracelet intermediate links, contrasting against satin-brushed titanium case middle, crown, and outer bracelet links. The Sapphire crystal front and back have anti-reflective coating, and the openworked sapphire dial reveals Caliber 7139's mechanical architecture—rhodium-plated movement components with pink gold accents on openworked oscillating weight, barrel bridge, and balance bridge creating warm contrast. The smoked transparent subdials maintain legibility while showcasing mechanism: day display at 9 o'clock with 24-hour indicator and red non-correction zone warning, large instantaneous jumping date aperture at 12 o'clock, month and leap year indication at 3 o'clock, astronomical moonphase at 6 o'clock. 18k pink gold applied hour markers and Royal Oak hands are filled with luminescent material. The self-winding Caliber 7139 measures 4.1mm thick, operates at 28,800 vph with a 55-hour power reserve.

Among collectors, the rose gold Tourbillon Souverain is prized for its early-era character, rarity, and its role in defining the aesthetic language that continues to shape F.P. Journe today.

items.model: F.P.Journe Tourbillon Souverain Vertical Ref. TV Platinum Salmon Dial
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Introduced in 2019 to celebrate the 20th anniversary of François-Paul Journe's first Tourbillon Souverain, the Vertical represents fundamental reimagining of the brand's signature complication. Where traditional tourbillons rotate horizontally—optimal for pocket watches positioned vertically—the Vertical's perpendicular orientation addresses wristwatch reality. Journe recognized wristwatches spend most time horizontal whether worn, resting on tables, or stored in boxes, rendering conventional tourbillons less effective against gravity. By positioning the tourbillon cage perpendicular to the movement at 90-degree angle to dial plane, amplitude remains constant whether watch lies flat or on its side. The Tourbillon Souverain's remontoir d'égalité made history in 1999 as first wristwatch incorporating constant-force device—mechanism delivering consistent power to escapement throughout power reserve. This combination earned the original Tourbillon Souverain the prestigious Aiguille d'Or prize at 2004 Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève. The salmon dial variant represents boutique-exclusive colorway rarely seen across F.P.Journe's typically conservative palette.

 42mm platinum case measures 13.6mm thick with polished surfaces and signature F.P.Journe stepped lugs. No traditional dial—instead, exposed 18k 4N rose gold movement bridges decorated with hand-engraved Clous de Paris guilloché pattern create visual backdrop. Hand-painted black inscriptions reading "F.P.Journe," "Invenit et Fecit," "Tourbillon Remontoir d'Égalité Seconde Morte" arc along dial periphery. Grand Feu white enamel subdial at 3 o'clock displays hours and minutes on single 18k white gold plate with applied Arabic numerals and blued steel hands—first time Journe utilized enamel dial, enabled by Vertical's increased case thickness. Small seconds subdial at 6 o'clock. Power reserve sector at 12 o'clock indicates 80-hour capacity. Vertical tourbillon aperture at 7 o'clock features mirror-polished cone-shaped ring concentrating light around cage. Manual-wind Caliber 1519 constructed entirely in 18k rose gold features vertical tourbillon completing revolution every 30 seconds—twice speed of traditional one-minute tourbillons for enhanced visual drama. Remontoir d'égalité (constant-force mechanism) delivers consistent torque to escapement. Free-sprung balance with four adjustable inertia weights, flat Anachron hairspring with Phillips overcoil operating at 21,600 vph. Sapphire crystal caseback reveals circular Geneva waves on baseplate, polished beveled screw heads. Light brown calfskin leather strap with platinum pin buckle.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Introduced in February 2023 initially as a UAE exclusive before global release in April, the salmon dial variant represents IWC's embrace of one of horology's most coveted color treatments. The Portugieser Automatic 40 itself debuted in 2020 as a modern interpretation of the legendary 1939 Reference 325—the watch that originated when two Portuguese businessmen requested a large wristwatch with pocket-watch precision. That original 41.5mm giant housed Caliber 74 pocket movement and sold merely 690 pieces between 1939 and 1981. The current 40mm diameter strikes the balance between vintage proportions and contemporary wearability while maintaining every design element that defined the Reference 325: streamlined dial with Arabic numerals, leaf-shaped hands, characteristic railway-track minute scale, and prominent small seconds at 6 o'clock. The salmon treatment exclusively sold through IWC boutiques and authorized dealers.

 The 40.4mm stainless steel case measures 12.4mm thick with alternating satin-brushed and polished surfaces throughout its construction. The domed sapphire crystal features anti-reflective coating on both sides. The refined salmon dial showcases sunray brushing that creates depth and warmth, complemented by rhodium-plated leaf-shaped hands and applied Arabic numeral hour markers. The characteristic railway-track minute scale encircles the dial, with small seconds subdial recessed at 6 o'clock. Powering the watch is manufacture Caliber 82200, featuring IWC's signature Pellaton bidirectional winding system invented in 1950 by technical director Albert Pellaton. The latest generation incorporates virtually wear-free zirconium oxide ceramic components for the pawls, automatic wheel, and heart-shaped cam. The movement operates at 28,800 vph with 60-hour power reserve and free-sprung balance. Black alligator leather strap with stainless steel butterfly folding clasp, sapphire exhibition caseback, 30-meter water resistance.

Gérald Genta's 1976  Nautilus revolutionized luxury watchmaking by proving stainless steel could command gold-watch pricing—a marketing gamble that shocked the industry and forever altered perceptions of sports watch value. The original "Jumbo" faced initial resistance due to its bold 42mm case ( Measuring 42mm across the widest point (including the “ears”)) , yet became the blueprint for integrated-bracelet luxury sports watches. items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Offshore   26062OR.OO.A002CA.01 'Alinghi Team' released in 2007 for the 32nd America's Cup, commemorating Audemars Piguet's sponsorship of Swiss sailing team Alinghi—who brought the America's Cup to Europe for the first time in 132 years with their 2003 victory. This marked numerous firsts for AP: first use of forged carbon bezel combined with precious metal case, first colored gasket (red silicone between bezel and case), first blackened hex bolts, first oversized rectangular pin buckle design. 

 The 44mm 18k rose gold case measures 14.3mm thick and features a forged carbon bezel secured by eight titanium screws with distinctive red silicone gasket visible between bezel and case. Ceramic crown and pushers complement the black lacquer dial, which showcases Méga Tapisserie guilloché at center surrounded by white luminescent rose gold Arabic numerals and skeleton hands. The dial's most distinctive element is the wedge-shaped 10-minute regatta countdown aperture spanning from 12 to 3 o'clock, which gradually turns red during the final minute before race start. Ship prow-shaped chronograph hands point to the Alinghi logo at 3 o'clock, a 20-minute register at 9, and 6-hour counter at 6. Inside beats Caliber 2326/2848 automatic movement—a JLC 899 base integrated with Dubois-Dépraz 2848 regatta module—featuring 50 jewels and 40-hour power reserve. The caseback bears an intricately engraved relief medallion depicting the Alinghi team in action.

 *This is an Alinghi Team Limited Edition of 600 pieces. 

 *This timepiece comes with an Open Paper, the original box, booklet, and 2021 AP Service Receipt.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Introduced in 1989 to replace the bulkier 16760 "Fat Lady," the 16710 represents the last generation of GMT-Master II with aluminum bezel inserts, produced until 2007. Collectors prize it as the perfect bridge between vintage and modern Rolex—retaining the slimmer 40mm case profile of classic five-digit references while incorporating contemporary features like sapphire crystal and improved movement technology. The "LN" designation signifies "Lunette Noir" (black bezel in French), the most understated variant compared to colorful Pepsi and Coke siblings. Throughout its 18-year production run, the reference underwent gradual evolution: tritium gave way to Luminova then Super-LumiNova around 1998-2000, hollow end links upgraded to solid in 2000, drilled lugs disappeared in 2003, and late examples received Caliber 3186 replacing 3185. 

 The 40mm stainless steel case features bidirectional rotating black aluminum bezel with 24-hour graduations, 120-click action. Black lacquer dial with white gold surrounds on luminescent hour markers, Mercedes hands, red 24-hour GMT hand. Date window at 3 o'clock with Cyclops magnification. This watch houses the Caliber 3185 automatic movement, independent quickset GMT hand enabling true three-timezone functionality. COSC-certified chronometer, 48-hour power reserve. Three-link Oyster bracelet with Oysterlock folding clasp, 100-meter water resistance. 

 *This timepiece comes with a Rolex Certified Pre-Owned Paper and Travel Case.

items.model: F.P.Journe Linesport Octa Sport Ref. ARS Titanium Grey Dial
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Born from Japanese collector Mori's 2011 request for an endurance racing watch, the  F.P. Journe LineSport Octa Sport launched in 2012 with revolutionary aluminum construction before transitioning to Grade 5 titanium in 2014 when aluminum proved insufficiently robust for daily wear. This earlier 42mm titanium generation (pre-2018 upgrade to 44mm) represents F.P. Journe's radical interpretation of sports watchmaking—combining haute independent horology with unexpected casualness. Rubber inserts protecting case sides, crown, and bracelet links function like automobile bumpers, absorbing shocks while creating distinctive visual signature. At approximately 65 grams total weight, it remains among the lightest full-bracelet titanium watches ever produced. The aluminum alloy movement marked Journe's first departure from signature 18k rose gold calibers, enabling featherweight construction while maintaining manufacture standards.

 The 42mm Grade 5 titanium case measures 11.6mm height with matte anthracite finish, rubber-protected sides. Aluminum alloy dial with applied luminescent Arabic numerals, sapphire small seconds counter at 6 o'clock. Large instantaneous jump date at 1 o'clock, day/night indicator at 9 o'clock (unique to Octa Sport), power reserve display at 10:30. Steel luminescent hour/minute hands, white steel and red lacquered titanium small hands. Caliber 1300.3 automatic movement entirely constructed in aluminum alloy, off-center titanium rotor with tungsten segment, 160-hour (5-day) power reserve. Integrated titanium bracelet with rubber inserts, rubber-coated folding clasp with micro-adjustment.

As part of Journe’s foundational tourbillon references, this model sits at the very beginning of his independent career, when production was extremely limited and each watch was deeply personal. The platinum case elevates the watch into Journe’s most exclusive metal category, a distinction the brand reserves for its most important creations.

 The silver dial showcases the signature off-center time display balanced against the exposed tourbillon at 9 o’clock, with the remontoir d’égalité and dead-seconds mechanism visible in motion. The layout is unmistakably Journe—functional, asymmetric, and intellectually driven rather than decorative. Subtle engraved text, heat-blued hands, and the restrained color palette reward collectors who value substance over flash. Among serious Journe collectors, the Tourbillon Souverain Ref. TN is prized for its early-era significance, mechanical honesty, and its role in defining what modern independent haute horlogerie would become.

Crafted in white gold and paired with a factory mother-of-pearl dial set with diamond hour markers, this reference pushes the Daytona beyond its motorsport origins into a more luxurious, statement-driven direction. items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Patek Philippe Nautilus 3700/11J is one of the most important and historically significant Nautilus references ever produced. As the original “Jumbo” case introduced in the late 1970s, the 3700 established Gérald Genta’s vision of a luxury sports watch in precious metal long before the concept became mainstream. Executed in yellow gold, this reference is far rarer than its stainless steel counterpart and represents an early, bold statement from Patek Philippe during the Nautilus’ formative years.

 The black ribbed dial is pure first-generation Nautilus, with applied yellow gold baton markers and matching hands that preserve the watch’s minimalist, architectural balance. The slim, monobloc-style case and integrated yellow gold bracelet define the unmistakable Nautilus profile, while the proportions remain exceptionally elegant by modern standards. The 3700/11J is coveted not just for its scarcity, but for its role as the purest expression of the original Nautilus concept—untouched, iconic, and foundational to the entire collection.

 *This timepiece comes with a photocopy of the original papers, and a Patek Philippe Travel Pouch.

Introduced after the yellow and white gold versions, the platinum 5070 is widely regarded by collectors as the most desirable execution of the series, distinguished immediately by its rich blue sunburst dial and discreet diamond set into the case at 6 o’clock — a subtle signature reserved for Patek Philippe platinum watches.

Crafted in platinum and produced in extremely small numbers, this Black Label execution features a deep black dial reserved exclusively for longtime F.P. Journe collectors, reinforcing its discreet, insider appeal. The twin time displays symbolize Journe’s rare success in harnessing resonance within a wristwatch—an achievement that remains virtually unmatched in contemporary horology.

 The matte black dial amplifies the watch’s architectural clarity, with silvered hands and numerals providing sharp contrast while maintaining a restrained, technical aesthetic. The dual balances, visible through the caseback, oscillate in harmony to improve rate stability when synchronized, reflecting Journe’s philosophical emphasis on precision over spectacle. Paired with a platinum case that adds reassuring heft without excess ornamentation, the RQ Black Label is a pure collector’s piece—valued less for flash and more for the depth of watchmaking thought it represents.

items.model: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Rectangular 6015BA Vintage 'Ladies' Yellow Gold Diamond-Set Quartz (1982)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
This vintage Audemars Piguet 6015BA Rectangular Royal Oak represents a lesser-seen but important chapter in the brand’s design history, when AP was actively experimenting beyond the Royal Oak while maintaining its emphasis on precious materials and refined finishing. The rectangular 24.5mm x 32.5mm case, executed in yellow gold and fully diamond-set, reflects a distinctly late-20th-century approach to luxury—geometric, elegant, and unapologetically jewelry-forward. Produced for a ladies’ clientele that valued both design and prestige, this reference showcases Audemars Piguet’s ability to translate haute horology aesthetics into compact, wearable forms.

 The champagne-toned dial is understated by comparison, allowing the diamond-set case and bracelet to remain the focal point, while applied diamond hour markers add subtle depth and cohesion. Powered by a quartz movement, the watch favors slimness, reliability, and ease of wear, consistent with high-jewelry Audemars Piguet pieces of the era. Today, vintage AP rectangular models like this are increasingly appreciated for their rarity, strong period character, and their role in broadening the brand’s identity beyond round and octagonal icons.

 *This timepiece comes with AP Digital Archive Papers.

Paired with a dark leather strap, the Ref. RN blends thoughtful complication, timeless finishing, and a considered aesthetic that feels timeless rather than showy.

items.sourceDescription:
The  Royal Oak transformed watchmaking when Gérald Genta designed it in 1972, establishing the luxury steel sports watch as a category and becoming Audemars Piguet's defining icon. Reference 15510ST represents the current Selfwinding 41mm execution in stainless steel, the configuration that most faithfully carries forward the spirit of the original — a precious-grade sports watch rendered in steel, finished to a standard typically reserved for gold. Introduced as the contemporary three-hand Royal Oak with the upgraded in-house Caliber 4302, this grey "Grande Tapisserie" version offers the model's most versatile and quietly contemporary face, prized by collectors for the enduring desirability that keeps steel Royal Oaks among the most sought-after watches in production.

 The 41mm case in stainless steel features the signature octagonal bezel secured by eight polished hexagonal screws, combining brushed and polished surfaces across the case and integrated bracelet. The grey "Grande Tapisserie" dial carries white gold applied hour markers and Royal Oak hands with luminescent coating, and a date aperture at three. The in-house self-winding Caliber 4302 — comprising 257 parts with a full balance bridge and 22-karat gold rotor — delivers a 70-hour power reserve, visible through the sapphire caseback. An integrated stainless steel bracelet with AP folding clasp completes the watch.

With a rectangular case around 27 mm x 37 mm and a diamond-set bezel, it stands out as a luxury wrist piece where design and complementarity matter as much as the brand name.

items.model: Patek Philippe Nautilus 5740/1G-001 Perpetual Calendar Moon Phases (2018)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Introduced in 2018, the 5740/1G marked a pivotal moment in the  Nautilus's history: the first Grand Complication ever housed within Gérald Genta's 1976 sports design. Patek Philippe accomplished what many considered impossible — fitting a perpetual calendar into the Nautilus silhouette while preserving the proportions that define the model. At 8.42mm thick, it remains the thinnest perpetual calendar Patek Philippe has ever produced. For collectors, the reference represents the convergence of the maison's most coveted sports line with its most historically significant complication, making it among the most pursued contemporary Nautilus references.

 The 40mm case in 18-karat white gold frames a sunburst blue dial with the signature horizontally embossed pattern and white gold applied baton hour markers. Three subdials at three, six, and nine o'clock display day, date, month, leap year cycle, moon phase , and 24-hour indication. The ultra-thin automatic Caliber 240 Q drives the perpetual calendar via a 22-karat gold micro-rotor, visible through the sapphire caseback. An integrated white gold bracelet with fold-over clasp completes the watch.

*This timepiece comes with a stylus.

Bvlgari, the storied Roman jeweler, has always fused watchmaking with bold Italian design, and few creations capture that spirit like the Tubogas . Named for the Italian term for gas pipe, its supple coiled bracelet is crafted without soldering, wrapping the wrist like a spring in a technique the maison perfected decades ago. Paired here with the double-logo Bvlgari-Bvlgari bezel, first conceived in the 1970s, it becomes a piece of sculptural jewelry that happens to tell time.

 Crafted in stainless steel, the watch coils around the wrist in three flexible rows of the signature tubogas bracelet, each polished band flowing seamlessly into the next. A small round case anchors one end, its bezel engraved with the double "BVLGARI BVLGARI" logo that became a brand hallmark. The black dial stays clean and legible, marked by baton indices, Arabic twelve and six, and slim hands. A quartz movement keeps it slender and carefree.

 *This timepiece has been serviced and polished by Bvlgari.
*Comes with two year factory warranty, valid until August 2028.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Richard Mille RM 65‑01 “McLaren W1” takes driver-focused design from the track to the wrist. Inspired by McLaren’s hypercar W1, the dynamically sculpted Carbon TPT and grade 5 titanium case measures 43.84 × 49.94 × 16.19 mm, echoing the car’s sculpted profile. Its skeletonized dial features architecture inspired by the W1’s wheel rims, with vibrant papaya-orange pushers, blue highlights, and a branded “Speedmark” crown. The ultra-slim dual-layer titanium bezel—just 0.5 mm at its thinnest—underscores the technical sophistication behind the case design. 

 Inside, the RMAC4 automatic split‑seconds chronograph movement runs at an elevated 5 Hz (36,000 vph), with double column wheels for smooth activation and a one-tenth-second display. It features a rapid-winding “jump‑start” pusher that immediately recharges the mainspring—an ideal mechanical nod to pit‑stop precision—while delivering a robust 60‑hour power reserve. Limited to 500 pieces, this highly engineered chronograph is a collector’s favorite—a technical powerhouse wrapped in avant-garde automotive style.

 *Limited Edition of 500 pieces.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Day-Date occupies the summit of Rolex's catalog as the "President" — introduced in 1956 as the first wristwatch to display both the date and the day of the week spelled out in full through separate apertures. Reserved exclusively for precious metals since its inception, the model earned its nickname through its distinctive President bracelet and its association with heads of state, statesmen, and cultural icons who elevated it to a status symbol without equal. Reference 228235 represents the modern 40mm execution in Everose gold — Rolex's proprietary rose gold alloy blended with platinum to preserve its warm hue against fading — dressed here with an olive green sunray dial with applied Roman numerals, a distinctive and contemporary interpretation of the Day-Date's dress-watch heritage.

 The 40mm Oyster case in 18-karat Everose gold features a fluted Everose gold bezel and Twinlock screw-down crown. The olive green sunray dial carries applied Everose gold Roman numeral hour markers, day aperture at twelve, date aperture at three beneath the Cyclops, and matching Everose gold hands. The in-house automatic Caliber 3255 — equipped with the Chronergy escapement, paramagnetic Parachrom hairspring, and Paraflex shock absorbers — delivers a 70-hour power reserve and Superlative Chronometer certification, completed by the signature President bracelet with semi-circular three-piece links in Everose gold and concealed folding Crownclasp.

*This timepiece comes with the original white hang tag.

Designed by Gérald Genta, it features a 42mm stainless steel case ( Measuring 42mm across the widest point (including the “ears”)) with its signature porthole-inspired design and integrated bracelet, marking a bold departure from traditional dress watches of the era.

Revered by collectors, the 3700/1A set the foundation for the luxury sports watch category and remains one of the most important and collectible Patek Philippe references of the 20th century.

items.model: Patek Philippe Nautilus 5712/1A-001 Stainless Steel Blue Dial Moon Phases (2022)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The 5712/1A-001 stands among the most distinctive and beloved  Nautilus   references ever produced, distinguished by its asymmetrical dial layout that has become iconic within Patek Philippe's catalog. Combining moon phase, date pointer, small seconds, and power reserve in a single ultra-thin steel Nautilus, it offers a complication set unmatched elsewhere in the collection. Discontinued in 2025 as part of Patek Philippe's strategic catalog refresh, the reference has since attained significantly elevated collectible status, prized for the harmonious balance of Gérald Genta's 1976 sports design with the contemplative elegance of celestial and astronomical indications — an unusual pairing that has secured its place among the most cerebral expressions of the Nautilus line.

 The 40mm case in stainless steel measures just 8.52mm thick, framed by the signature rounded octagonal bezel with alternating satin and polished finishes. The black-blue gradient dial with horizontal embossing displays the asymmetric layout: moon phase and date pointer at seven, small seconds at four, and power reserve indicator between ten and eleven. The self-winding Caliber 240 PS IRM C LU — an ultra-thin movement with 22-karat gold micro-rotor and Patek Philippe Seal certification — delivers 48 hours of reserve, completed by an integrated stainless steel Nautilus bracelet with fold-over clasp.

 *This model was discontinued in 2025.

 *This timepiece has an old-style clasp, and comes with the original stylus and hang tag.

 The 40mm case in 950 platinum features a distinctive chestnut brown Cerachrom ceramic bezel with engraved tachymetric scale — a warm contrast against the cool platinum case — paired with Triplock screw-down crown and pushers. The ice blue sunburst dial carries baguette-cut diamond hour markers, three tonal ice blue subdials arranged at three, six, and nine, red "Daytona" text above the six o'clock subdial, and blued white gold hands. The in-house automatic Caliber 4130 delivers a 72-hour power reserve and Superlative Chronometer certification, completed by a 950 platinum Oyster bracelet with Oysterlock folding safety clasp.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Cartier Tank à Guichets WGTA0236 is a modern tribute to one of Cartier’s most enigmatic designs, reintroduced in platinum for 2025 with a focus on architectural minimalism and horological purity. With no traditional dial, hands, or numerals, the solid brushed platinum case features only two discreet apertures: one at the top for the jumping hour and one below for the trailing minutes. This mysterious time display, originally conceived in 1928, embodies Cartier’s avant-garde spirit and mastery of design reduction.

 Powered by a manual-winding mechanical movement, the complication delivers instantaneous hour jumps and smooth minute progression—visible only when needed. The platinum case exudes weight and elegance, while the clean geometry of the Tank form is emphasized by its unadorned surface. Paired with an alligator leather strap and a platinum folding buckle, the WGTA0236 is a connoisseur’s timepiece—bold in concept, subtle in execution, and a pure expression of Cartier’s legacy in both form and function.

items.sourceDescription:

Housed in a 42mm case crafted from Tungsten carbide with tantalum elements —the watch features a stealthy, sculptural profile that contrasts beautifully with its minimalist dial presentation. This reference is equipped with the robust Valjoux 727 movement—a hand-wound caliber prized for its reliability and precision during an era before automatic chronographs became the norm.

The matte black dial, paired with contrasting silver subdials, exudes classic motorsport styling, while the crisp white printing and simple baton markers reflect the clean, utilitarian aesthetic that made vintage Daytonas so iconic. Today, the 6265 is highly sought after by collectors for its pure, tool-watch DNA and its place at the crossroads of Rolex’s transition from vintage to modern chronograph design.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Patek Philippe 5308G-001 is a monumental achievement in high horology, introduced in 2025 as the brand’s most technically complex wristwatch currently in production. Crafted in white gold, this  Grand Complication houses four of Patek Philippe’s most prestigious mechanisms in a single, elegantly balanced timepiece: a minute repeater, a split-seconds monopusher chronograph , and an instantaneous perpetual calendar . The 42mm case is imposing yet refined, with polished white gold surfaces and a sapphire caseback that reveals the exceptional finishing of the R CHR 27 PS QI movement—featuring 799 components, 12 patents, and a 65-hour power reserve.

 The watch is distinguished by its radiant ice blue opaline dial. The dial layout is masterfully symmetrical, with twin day/month apertures at 12 o’clock, date and moonphase at 6, and dual chronograph subdials at 3 and 9 o’clock. Leaf-shaped white gold hands and applied hour markers complete the elegant visual composition. With all calendar indications advancing instantaneously at midnight, and the split-seconds chronograph controlled by a single pusher, the 5308G-001 is not just a showcase of complications—it’s a mechanical tour de force, representing the pinnacle of modern Patek Philippe watchmaking.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The 5712/1A-001 stands among the most distinctive and beloved  Nautilus references ever produced, distinguished by its asymmetrical dial layout that has become iconic within Patek Philippe's catalog. Combining moon phase, date pointer, small seconds, and power reserve in a single ultra-thin steel Nautilus, it offers a complication set unmatched elsewhere in the collection. Discontinued in 2025 as part of Patek Philippe's strategic catalog refresh, the reference has since attained significantly elevated collectible status, prized for the harmonious balance of Gérald Genta's 1976 sports design with the contemplative elegance of celestial and astronomical indications — an unusual pairing that has secured its place among the most cerebral expressions of the Nautilus line.

 The 40mm case in stainless steel measures just 8.52mm thick, framed by the signature rounded octagonal bezel with alternating satin and polished finishes. The black-blue gradient dial with horizontal embossing displays the asymmetric layout: moon phase and date pointer at seven, small seconds at four, and power reserve indicator between ten and eleven. The self-winding Caliber 240 PS IRM C LU — an ultra-thin movement with 22-karat gold micro-rotor and Patek Philippe Seal certification — delivers 48 hours of reserve, completed by an integrated stainless steel Nautilus bracelet with fold-over clasp.

 *This model was discontinued in 2025.

 *This timepiece has an old-style clasp, and comes with the original stylus.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Introduced in 2018, the 5740/1G marked a pivotal moment in the  Nautilus's history: the first Grand Complication ever housed within Gérald Genta's 1976 sports design. Patek Philippe accomplished what many considered impossible — fitting a perpetual calendar into the Nautilus silhouette while preserving the proportions that define the model. At 8.42mm thick, it remains the thinnest perpetual calendar Patek Philippe has ever produced. For collectors, the reference represents the convergence of the maison's most coveted sports line with its most historically significant complication, making it among the most pursued contemporary Nautilus references.

 The 40mm case in 18-karat white gold frames a sunburst blue dial with the signature horizontally embossed pattern and white gold applied baton hour markers. Three subdials at three, six, and nine o'clock display day, date, month, leap year cycle, moon phase , and 24-hour indication. The ultra-thin automatic Caliber 240 Q drives the perpetual calendar via a 22-karat gold micro-rotor, visible through the sapphire caseback. An integrated white gold bracelet with fold-over clasp completes the watch.

 *This timepiece has a new style clasp, but does not have the micro adjustment.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Among the rarest  Daytonas ever produced, the 116576TBR was created exclusively for the Middle Eastern market. The blued Eastern Arabic numerals distinguish this reference from all other platinum Daytonas, elevating it beyond even the typical platinum model's exclusivity. Introduced at Baselworld 2014, this represents the intersection of Rolex's chronograph heritage with bespoke cultural design, honoring Middle Eastern collectors with region-specific numerals while maintaining the Daytona's legendary racing pedigree. The ice blue dial—reserved exclusively for platinum Rolex models—combined with Eastern Arabic script creates one of the most unobtainable configurations in modern Rolex production.

 The 40mm case is crafted entirely from 950 platinum, distinguished by its soft, regal luster that contrasts sharply with steel or gold. Thirty-six baguette-cut diamonds encircle the bezel in a flawless arrangement, set within the polished platinum frame that slopes elegantly toward the dial. The ice blue dial features applied blued Eastern Arabic numerals and matching blue subdials at 3, 6, and 9 o'clock that track elapsed time. Inside beats the automatic Caliber 4130 with vertical clutch chronograph mechanism, Parachrom hairspring for shock resistance, and 72-hour power reserve. The platinum Oyster bracelet features solid links and Oysterlock folding clasp.

items.model: Richard Mille RM 30-01 Declutchable Rotor Rose Gold Titanium (2024)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
Richard Mille built a revolution on treating the wristwatch like a Formula 1 chassis, and the  RM 30-01 distills that philosophy into a single clever idea: a declutchable rotor. When the mainspring reaches full charge, the winding system physically disengages to spare the movement from unnecessary stress, then re-engages as the reserve runs down, its status shown by an ON/OFF indicator. Collectors prize Richard Mille for exactly this fusion of motorsport engineering and unrepentant technical theater.

 The tonneau case pairs a rose gold bezel and caseband with a titanium middle section, secured by Richard Mille's exposed spline screws. Within, the skeletonized in-house automatic caliber sprawls across the dial in grey titanium bridges, hovering skeleton hands tracing the hours. An oversized date sits near four o'clock, a function selector reads H, D, or W, and the ON/OFF clutch indicator watches over it all. A grey rubber strap completes the cockpit-like presentation.

items.model: Rolex Day-Date 40 228348RBR Yellow Gold Green Roman Numeral Dial Diamond Bezel (2022)
items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The Rolex Day-Date  has held its position as Rolex's flagship statement piece since 1956, the first wristwatch to display both day and date in full, and produced exclusively in precious metals throughout its history. Reference 228348RBR represents the gem-set expression of the modern 40mm generation in 18-karat yellow gold, distinguished by a factory diamond-set bezel — the "RBR" suffix denoting this configuration. Dressed here with a vivid green lacquer dial bearing gold Roman numerals, the reference appeals to collectors drawn to the convergence of the Day-Date's enduring presidential status with bold dial coloration and factory diamond setting, a combination that has performed strongly among contemporary gem-set Rolex production.

 The 40mm case in 18-karat yellow gold carries a bezel set with brilliant-cut diamonds and frames a green lacquer dial with applied gold Roman numerals, day aperture at twelve, and date at three beneath the Cyclops magnifier. The in-house automatic Caliber 3255 — equipped with the Chronergy escapement, Parachrom hairspring, and Paraflex shock absorbers — delivers a 70-hour power reserve and Superlative Chronometer certification. The watch is completed by a solid yellow gold President bracelet with semi-circular three-piece links and concealed folding Crownclasp.

 *This timepiece has factory stickers on the sides of the case, caseback, and the buckle.

items.sourceDescription:
The  Code 11.59 represents Audemars Piguet's boldest modern gamble: a contemporary round watch conceived to stand as a third pillar alongside the Royal Oak and its Offshore sibling. Divisive at its 2019 debut, the collection has steadily won admirers who appreciate its architectural ambition and refusal to trade on nostalgia. This reference marks a significant moment, arriving in stainless steel rather than the precious metals that first defined the line, making one of watchmaking's most intriguing designs newly accessible.

 The 41mm case reveals the collection's defining complexity: an octagonal middle section set between a round bezel and caseband, with slender openworked lugs and a double-curved sapphire crystal bending light across the dial. That dial glows in smoked green, its center worked in a guilloché that radiates outward beneath applied white-gold markers and a date at three o'clock. A tonal green textile strap completes a watch both classical and unmistakably modern.

items.description: Presented for private inquiry. Please confirm the exact available piece, condition, documentation and price.
items.sourceDescription:
The  Royal Oak 16202BA represents the contemporary evolution of Audemars Piguet's most iconic design, maintaining the beloved Jumbo proportions that defined Gérald Genta's revolutionary 1972 original reference 5402 while incorporating the latest manufacture movement technology. Introduced in 2022 as the successor to the 50th Anniversary model, this reference continues the legacy of the extra-thin Royal Oak Jumbo showcasing Audemars Piguet's mastery in creating ultra-thin automatic movements while preserving the architectural purity and balanced proportions that made the original Jumbo a legend. The smoked yellow gold-toned dial with gradient effect creates stunning visual depth that shifts dramatically depending on lighting conditions, offering collectors the warm aesthetic of precious metal execution combined with contemporary dial artistry, appealing to those who appreciate understated luxury with heritage significance in current production form backed by Audemars Piguet's comprehensive warranty and global service network.

 The 39mm case crafted in 18-karat yellow gold features the iconic octagonal bezel secured by eight polished hexagonal screws in white gold, brushed surfaces with polished beveled edges creating dynamic interplay of finishes, integrated case construction with screwed caseback, glare-proofed sapphire crystal and exhibition sapphire caseback revealing the meticulously finished automatic movement. The smoked yellow gold-toned dial displays the signature Petite Tapisserie pattern with gradient effect transitioning from lighter center to darker periphery, applied polished yellow gold baton hour markers with luminescent coating, yellow gold Royal Oak hands with luminescent coating, fine printed minute track, and date window at 3 o'clock. Inside beats the self-winding Caliber 7121 manufactured entirely in-house featuring ultra-thin construction at 3.4mm height, 18-karat rose gold skeletonized rotor, 33 jewels, 268 components, frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour, and approximately 52 hours of power reserve. Integrated 18-karat yellow gold bracelet with brushed surfaces and polished beveled edges secured with AP folding clasp.
